title: TICRR orchestrates mitochondrial dynamics and tumor-endothelial crosstalk to drive radioresistance in colorectal cancer.
abstract: Radiotherapy resistance remains a major challenge in the clinical management of colorectal cancer (CRC), highlighting the urgent need to identify novel regulators of radiosensitivity. Here, we reveal a multi-layered mechanism whereby TICRR drives CRC radioresistance. TICRR is significantly upregulated in radioresistant CRC tissues and cell lines and is associated with poor patient survival. TICRR knockdown suppresses tumor cell proliferation, impairs DNA damage repair, and enhances radiosensitivity both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, TICRR functions as an RNA-binding protein (RBP) to stabilize the mitochondrial protein C1QBP mRNA, thereby maintaining mitochondrial function and regulating AMP levels, which in turn modulate the AMPK/HIF pathway and VEGFA transcription. TICRR-high tumor cells interact with endothelial cells via the VEGFA-VEGFR1 signaling axis and transfer mitochondria to endothelial cells to enhance angiogenesis, a process disrupted by TICRR downregulation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that TICRR promotes CRC radioresistance through a multi-layered mechanism involving mitochondrial function and tumor-endothelial cell communication, highlighting TICRR inhibition as a potential strategy for radiosensitization.

title: Efficient G-Quadruplex RNA Resolution Mediated by Dimeric Suv3 Helicase.
abstract: G-quadruplexes (G4) are stable secondary structures that can impede DNA replication, transcription, and translation. Although the human mitochondrial helicase Suv3 (SUPV3L1) is essential for RNA unwinding in mitochondrial RNA decay pathways, its involvement in resolving G4-RNA remains poorly characterized. Here, we demonstrate that dimeric Suv3 binds G4-RNA with nanomolar affinity, independently of ATP and irrespective of a 3' overhang. However, efficient catalytic resolution of G4-RNA by Suv3 requires both ATP hydrolysis and a minimum 3' single-stranded overhang of approximately 12 nucleotides to serve as a loading dock. Our findings support a translocation-based mechanism whereby efficient G4 resolution is initiated by the binding of Suv3 to G4-RNA with a long 3' overhang, and this interaction triggers ATP hydrolysis, subsequent enzyme translocation, and G4 unfolding. We further show that dimeric Suv3 is markedly more effective than its monomeric counterpart in resolving G4-RNA, particularly under physiologically relevant mitochondrial salt conditions. Structural modeling supports that dimeric Suv3 functions as an asymmetric complex, with one of the subunits together with the C-terminal tails interacting with the G4 core structure, while the other subunit tethers the long 3' overhang to enhance enzymatic efficiency and processivity. Together, these results establish Suv3 as a mitochondrial G4-RNA resolvase and provide a mechanistic framework for understanding how Suv3 dysfunction is linked to aberrant RNA processing in mitochondria and disease.

title: N6-methyladenosine reader IGF2BP3 promotes endometrial cancer progression via modification of circ-EPB41L2 expression.
abstract: Endometrial cancer is one of the primary contributors to cancer-related mortality on a global scale. Insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA binding protein 3 (IGF2BP3) is a reader protein of N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modifications and serves a key role in the carcinogenesis of numerous solid tumors. The present study explored the role and underlying mechanism of IGF2BP3 in endometrial cancer. Bioinformatics methods were applied to examine m6A reader protein expression levels and their effect on survival. Reverse transcription-quantitative PCR and western blotting were used to determine IGF2BP3 expression in cancer and paracancerous tissues. After knockdown of IGF2BP3 expression, cell proliferation and migration were examined. Significantly expressed genes were identified through Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes and Gene Ontology analysis. Additionally, the cross-linking immunoprecipitation followed by high-throughput sequencing (CLIP-seq) database and methylated RNA immunoprecipitation (MeRIP) techniques were employed to ascertain the targets of IGF2BP3. The present study revealed that the expression levels of IGF2BP1, IGF2BP3, RNA binding motif protein 15 and YTH N6-methyladenosine RNA binding protein C2 differed between normal and endometrial cancer tissue, based on The Cancer Genome Atlas analysis. Through examination of endometrial cancer tissues and Kaplan-Meier analysis, IGF2BP3 was determined to be a target for further research. Following knockdown of IGF2BP3 expression in HEC-1A cells using short hairpin RNA transfection, proliferation and migration were decreased compared with those in the control group. A transcriptome-wide RNA-sequencing assay indicated that circular RNA (circ) was abnormally expressed in endometrial carcinoma and was regulated by IGF2BP3. CLIP-seq database analysis and MeRIP suggested that circ-erythrocyte membrane protein band 4.1 like-2 (EPB41L2) was the target of IGF2BP3. IGF2BP3 was involved in the progression of endometrial cancer and served an oncogenic role by targeting circ-EPB41L2 in an m6A-dependent manner.

title: G-quadruplex nucleic acid structures: form, function, regulation, and therapeutic targeting.
abstract: G-quadruplexes (G4s) are non-canonical nucleic acid structures formed by guanine-rich DNA and RNA sequences that regulate genome and transcriptome function. Once regarded as little more than an in vitro curiosity, G4s are now understood to be widespread features of cellular nucleic acids that influence transcription, DNA replication, translation, telomere maintenance, chromatin organization, and genome stability. Their formation is governed by sequence context, monovalent cations, molecular crowding, and an extensive network of G4-binding proteins and helicases that coordinate folding and resolution according to cellular need. Here, we review the current understanding of G4 biology, from molecular structure to therapeutic application. We cover the structural diversity of DNA, RNA, and hybrid DNA:RNA G4s; their roles in gene regulation, replication, and RNA metabolism; the mechanisms by which helicases and other G4-binding proteins recognize, remodel, and resolve these structures; and the experimental approaches that established their existence and function in living cells. We also discuss the rapidly expanding therapeutic landscape, including small-molecule G4 stabilizers and destabilizers, synthetic-lethal strategies that exploit DNA repair deficiencies, and G4-based aptamers and other emerging modalities. Collectively, the evidence supports a view of G4s as dynamic conformational switches, with their biological effects arising from the balance between folding and resolution. Understanding how this balance is established, and how it goes wrong, has broad implications for genome regulation, human disease, and the development of new therapeutic strategies.

title: NSUN2 siRNA combined with cisplatin promotes ferroptosis and inhibits the proliferation of cervical cancer cells by downregulating GOLPH3 expression.
abstract: Cisplatin resistance presents a major obstacle to effective treatment of cervical cancer (CC). Inducing ferroptosis represents a promising strategy to overcome cisplatin resistance. Thus, we aim to investigate the regulatory role of GOLPH3 in ferroptosis and its underlying mechanisms. Gene and protein expression were detected using RT-qPCR and western blot. CCK-8 and colony formation assays were used for cell viability and proliferation measurement. Lipid peroxidation levels were detected using the C11-BODIPY fluorescent probe via flow cytometry, and MDA content was measured by a commercial kit. RIP and MeRIP assays were applied to validate RNA-protein binding and m⁵C modification, respectively. Our results showed that GOLPH3 knockdown enhanced erastin- or cisplatin-induced ferroptosis in CC cells, and GOLPH3 knockdown-induced ferroptosis in cisplatin-treated CC cells was reversed by Fer-1, indicating that GOLPH3 knockdown inhibits cell proliferation via promoting ferroptosis. Besides, GOLPH3 depletion suppressed the AKT/GSK3β/NRF2 pathway, thereby enhancing ferroptosis. Furthermore, NSUN2 mediated m⁵C modification of GOLPH3 mRNA and recruited ALYREF to enhance its stability. NSUN2 knockdown downregulated GOLPH3 expression. Furthermore, NSUN2 knockdown augmented cisplatin-induced growth inhibition of parental and cisplatin-resistant CC cells through enhanced ferroptosis, whereas GOLPH3 overexpression reversed this effect. In conclusion, our findings suggest that NSUN2 may stabilize GOLPH3 mRNA via m⁵C modification in an ALYREF-dependent manner, which may activate the AKT/GSK3β/NRF2 pathway to inhibit ferroptosis and potentially contribute to cisplatin resistance in CC.

title: Ultrasensitive Regulation in the Tryptophan System in Escherichia coli Provides Effective Noise Mitigation
abstract: The tryptophan system in Escherichia coli maintains intracellular concentration of tryptophan in a narrow band regardless of the nutritional status and uncertainty in its environment. The system is characterized by three distinct regulations namely, genetic regulation, mRNA attenuation and enzyme inhibition, that use the tryptophan concentration as a feedback signal. It has been shown previously, that the multiple feedback loop design is responsible for rapid synthesis of tryptophan when faced with starvation. It is well known that a design with rapid response to external signals also implies poorer noise mitigation properties. This work investigates the design elements that limit the adverse impact of the multiple feedback loop architecture on noise propagation in the tryptophan system using a frequency response analysis. Specifically, we use sinusoidal input describing functions to approximate the transfer characteristics of the ultrasensitive regulators and then obtain the frequency response of the closed-loop feedback system. The study suggests that the tryptophan system of E. coli has evolved to simultaneously satisfy the two properties of rapid response and noise mitigation. Particularly, the multiple feedback loop is responsible for the rapid response, while the nonlinear regulation provides effective noise mitigation.

title: Endosomal mRNA transport coordinates local mitochondrial bioenergetics during polar fungal growth.
abstract: Mitochondrial function relies on the precise spatial coordination of protein synthesis and import. Most mitochondrial proteins are nuclear-encoded and must be supplied across varying intracellular distances. In highly polarized cells such as fungal hyphae and neurons, active long-distance mRNA transport is thought to sustain distal mitochondrial function, but its mechanistic coupling to protein import and organelle physiology is unclear. Here, we demonstrate that endosomal transport of mRNAs encoding mitochondrial proteins orchestrates local bioenergetics in infectious hyphae of Ustilago maydis. Using the subunit Atp3 of electron transport chain Complex V as a model, we uncover that the endosomal mRNA transporter Rrm4 is required for efficient mitochondrial protein import, particularly at growth poles. Loss of Rrm4 leads to defects in mitochondrial import, resulting in altered physiology. We propose that endosome-coupled mRNA transport constitutes a fundamental layer of subcellular mitochondrial homeostasis, with implications extending from fungal pathogenicity to neuronal disease.
extra: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A

title: Domain-encoded DNA barcodes for combinatorial multiplexed protein imaging via stepwise displacement.
abstract: Multiplexed protein imaging via DNA barcoding faces a fundamental scaling constraint: Each target requires a distinct DNA identity, making barcode capacity grow only linearly with the number of validated sequences. Combinatorial encoding in RNA fluorescence in situ hybridization achieves exponential scaling by distributing shared readout sequences across dozens of probes per transcript, but antibody-based protein labeling lacks this multiprobe architecture. Here, we report domain-encoded DNA barcodes (DEDBs), which embed combinatorial identity within the internal domain organization of a single-stranded DNA scaffold. Three orthogonal encoding units arranged across three encoding domains define a theoretical design space of 27 barcodes. Sequence reuse does not compromise readout specificity: Each read strand spans two adjacent domains, so a mismatched read strand inevitably contains a continuous stretch of noncomplementary bases and forms a thermodynamically disfavored intermediate that is subsequently displaced by the perfectly matched strand. We term this self-correcting behavior thermodynamic proofreading, and a three-process kinetic model shows that specificity arises not from initial binding discrimination but from cognate-driven correction at the product level. Coupled with signal-amplified antibody labeling, DEDBs enable quantitatively decoded nine-target intracellular protein imaging in fixed cells. The same barcode library supports Polychrome trajectory decoding for combinatorial identification and Monochrome cycle-resolved visualization for direct single-target inspection through reconfiguration of read-strand labeling. By generating combinatorial identities through the positional arrangement of reusable sequences within a single DNA strand, DEDBs reframe DNA barcode design from sequence enumeration to positional encoding.
extra: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A

title: Engineering Tunable Helper Lipid Architecture to Improve Messenger RNA Lipid Nanoparticle Performance.
abstract: Helper lipids are essential structural components of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), yet systematic design principles linking helper lipid architecture to messenger RNA (mRNA) delivery performance remain poorly defined. Here we identify helper lipid architecture as a major, largely unexplored design lever for optimizing LNP performance. Using a modular library of more than 80 rationally designed helper lipids, we show that systematic variation in headgroup chemistry, linker topology, and tail cardinality reshapes both LNP biophysical behavior and biological performance. Martini molecular dynamics (MD) simulations combined with multimodal structural analyses reveal that high-performing scaffolds undergo a pH-dependent transition into fusogenic inverse hexagonal-like ordering, substantially lowering the energetic barrier for endosomal escape. These performance gains persist across the clinically relevant ALC-0315 and DLin-MC3-DMA platforms, establishing helper lipid architecture as a transferable design parameter across distinct ionizable lipid chemistries. Translating these design principles into function, optimized helper lipid formulations restore hepatic protein expression in a mouse model of ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency and increase antigen expression and immunogenicity in both preclinical models and in the in vitro human MIMIC platform. Together, these findings establish helper lipids as tunable molecular actuators of potency, tolerability, and stability, offering an engineering framework for next-generation mRNA vaccines and therapeutics.

title: A dual biocontainment system specifically constraining the transfer and escape of the engineered plasmid in microbial communities.
abstract: A variety of engineered genetic elements and circuits enable bacteria to sense environmental signals, process information, and execute programmed biological functions. However, the potential escape from such synthetic constructs into the natural environment poses biosafety risks and could disrupt ecological balance. To address this, we developed a dual biocontainment system designed to restrict the replication and expression of engineered plasmids exclusively within modified host (TEV protease and sgRNA-dCas9). This system employs TEV protease to remove ssrA degradation tags fused to the plasmid replication protein RepA, thereby enabling plasmid replication. Concurrently, a specific guide RNA (sgRNA) forms an inhibitory complex with dCas9 to prevent cleavage of the engineered plasmid by the I-OnuI endonuclease. Overall, dual biocontainment system provides a robust safety tool both in vitro and in vivo to restrict the transfer and escape of engineered plasmids (with an escape rate of 4.4 × 10-8 in vitro and 2.4 × 10-8 in vivo), giving an efficient platform for safely use of synthetic genetic elements.

title: Piperine Nanoparticles Significantly Improved Fragile X-Associated Tremor/Ataxia Syndrome via Mitigating RNA and Repeat-Associated Non-AUG Toxicities.
abstract: Fragile X-associated tremor/ataxia syndrome (FXTAS) is a neurodegenerative disorder driven by fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein 1 (FMR1) premutation CGG repeats on the X chromosome, causing RNA and repeat-associated non-AUG (RAN) toxicities. Although piperine demonstrated preliminary mitigation of RNA toxicity, its poor aqueous solubility restricted further development. The current study evaluated piperine nanoparticles (PIP NPs) with enhanced solubility for FXTAS management. Briefly, PIP NPs were prepared using flash nanoprecipitation followed by assessing their impact on both CGG repeat Drosophila and mouse models. PIP NPs could significantly ameliorate the climbing deficits, protect against early-stage mortality (100 μM) and preserve retinal integrity in CGG repeat Drosophila, and rescue motor coordination and abnormal learning conditioning in CGG repeat mice, while reducing toxic FMR1 mRNA, restoring Drosophila fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein 1 (dFmr1) or fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein (FMRP) expression, suppressing FMRpolyG-GFP production in Drosophila, and mitigating ubiquitin-positive intranuclear inclusions. Based on the findings, molecular docking analyses were adopted to provide a computational structural rationale for the proposed interactions between piperine and DExH-box helicase 9 (DHX9)/death-associated protein 5 (DAP5)/heat shock protein 70 (Hsp70). The serial in vitro, in vivo, and in silico investigations consistently demonstrated PIP NPs as a promising therapeutic candidate for FXTAS.

title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluations of Constrained Ugi Adducts as Anti-JEV Agents.
abstract: Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV) remains a major global health threat, with no approved antiviral therapeutics currently available. In this study, we exploited the versatility of the Ugi four-component reaction (U4CR) to design and synthesize a library of more than 70 novel conformationally constrained Ugi adducts. By systematically incorporating carbocyclic and heterocyclic ketones, we restricted the conformational flexibility of the Ugi scaffold to optimize interactions with viral replication machinery. Comprehensive structure-activity relationship studies led to the identification of 5g, 5h, 6b, 6q, and 7an as potent inhibitors of JEV replication, exhibiting submicromolar antiviral activity (5g, IC50 = 1.79 ± 0.13 μM; 5h, IC50 = 0.76 ± 0.01; 6b, IC50 = 1.37 ± 0.15 μM; 6q, IC50 = 1.02 ± 0.89; 7an, IC50 = 1.45 ± 0.17 μM) with good selectivity indexes (>72) and a favorable safety profile in Vero cells. Importantly, phospholipidosis assays demonstrated that the antiviral activity of 6b is not associated with phospholipid accumulation, indicating that its antiviral effects are unlikely to result from nonspecific phospholipidosis. A preliminary molecular docking study against conserved JEV nonstructural proteins, including RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), helicase, and protease, suggested that these conformationally constrained Ugi adducts represent a promising chemotype targeting RdRp for the development of potent antiviral agents against JEV.

title: Impact of ionic strength on the stability of dopamine-RNA complexes: a combined experimental and computational insight.
abstract: In this study, we have combined fluorescence spectroscopy with molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the impact of ionic strength on the binding of dopamine to single-stranded RNA. The MD simulation estimates the minimum free energy of binding to the specific, highest-affinity sites, whereas fluorescence spectroscopy reports the free energy of the ensemble of DOP molecules bound to single-stranded (ss-) polynucleotides, and the two methods are complementary to each other. Both the experimental and simulation results demonstrate that dopamine binds to ss-polynucleotides with notable sequence and structural selectivity, but with distinct trends. According to the experimental results, dopamine exhibits a higher affinity toward ss-poly(A) than toward ss-poly(U) at low ionic strength (0.02 M). Increasing the ionic strength to 0.150 M reverses this trend, enhancing the affinity toward ss-poly(U). MD simulations clearly show that the distance between the centers of mass of poly(A) and poly(U) changes from about 6 nm at low ionic strength to about 2 nm at high ionic strength for both poly(A) and poly(U). The radius of gyrations of the whole system of poly(A) and poly(U) changes from 3.5 nm to 1.75 nm in the same range of ionic strengths of the solution. These results clearly signal that increasing ionic strength to physiological levels promotes the formation of a complex between poly(A) and poly(U), which is not a double-stranded (ds-) helix but just a compact structure. The free energy of the most stable DOP-poly(U) complex formation is lower than that for the DOP-poly(A) at low ionic strengths and vice versa for the high ionic strengths. The combined experimental and computational findings highlight that the structural state of RNA and the electrostatic environment critically determine dopamine-RNA interactions, providing new insights into neurotransmitter-nucleic acid recognition mechanisms.

title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of whelk Neptunea cumingii (Crosse, 1862).
abstract: The whelk Neptunea cumingii (Crosse, 1862) is a cold-temperate marine gastropod with direct development, an atypical life-history trait that influences its dispersal and adaptation. Here, we present the first chromosome-level genome assembly of N. cumingii, produced by integrating Nanopore long reads, Illumina short reads, and Hi-C scaffolds data. The assembled genome spans 4,898.96 Mb with 37 pseudochromosomes and exhibits high heterozygosity (1.18%) and a substantial repetitive content (84.31%). The assembly achieves contig and scaffold N50 values of 6.50 Mb and 150.98 Mb, respectively, and contains 19,107 protein-coding genes along with comprehensive non-coding RNA annotations. This high-quality genomic resource provides a foundation for investigating the genetic basis of direct development and adaptation in marine mollusks.

title: Saponins and Sapogenins in Inflammation Therapeutics: Glycosylation-Dependent Mechanisms, Pharmacokinetics and Advanced Delivery Solutions.
abstract: Saponins and their aglycones, the sapogenins, are the bioactive constituents of medicinal herbs such as Panax ginseng and Astragalus membranaceus, and they act on inflammation at several levels at once. The canonical nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-κB), mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), and NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome cascades are the best-replicated entry points, and beyond them these compounds modify non-coding RNA networks and post-translational regulation and reshape immuno-metabolic circuits by suppressing glycolytic enzymes and engaging AMPK-dependent energy sensing. Whether a given activity belongs to the glycoside or to the aglycone is often unclear, because orally administered glycosides are extensively deglycosylated by the intestinal microbiota, and this review therefore organises the evidence by glycosylation status and annotates every compound accordingly. Translation is constrained by poor aqueous solubility, low and variable bioavailability, structural instability, and dose-dependent toxicity, and stimulus-responsive nanocarriers, exosome-based systems, and microbiota-aware pharmacokinetic modelling are the most credible routes past these barriers. The mechanistic picture that emerges is coherent but still provisional, and progress now depends less on further pathway catalogues than on experiments that establish direct target engagement and on pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic data obtained in human-relevant models.

title: Construction of minigenomic replicon and infectious virus-like particle systems for Ebola virus with epitope-tagged L polymerase.
abstract: Ebola virus (EBOV) L protein is the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) and a key antiviral target. Functional dissection of L during infection is hampered by scarce specific anti-L antibodies and mandatory BSL-4 containment for live EBOV. Here, we established two BSL-2 reverse genetic systems harboring tagged L protein to address these obstacles. First, we generated stable EBOV minigenomic replicon cells constitutively expressing NP, VP30, VP35 and TagL, supporting sustained viral minigenome replication. Second, we developed an infectious virus-like particle (iVLP) system in which an EBOV subgenome encoding GP, VP40 and VP24 replicates robustly in optimized TagL-expressing helper cells to generate fully infectious iVLPs, recapitulating the entire EBOV life cycle. Proteomic analysis of intact iVLPs and delipidated ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complexes uncovered a previously unrecognized association between EBOV RNP and cytoskeletal proteins. Pharmacological disruption of microtubules enhanced EBOV replication/transcription and virion production, providing new insights into virus-host interactions during EBOV infection. Collectively, these optimized TagL-integrated reverse genetics tools provide tractable BSL-2 tools to study EBOV L-RNP biology during the full viral life cycle.

title: Intrinsic disorder and phase separation propensity across diverse parasite proteomes.
abstract: Intrinsic protein disorder and liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) propensity are associated with diverse protein functions, yet their distribution across parasite proteomes remains incompletely characterized. We compared predicted intrinsic disorder and LLPS propensity across 13 parasite/pathogen proteomes and two non-parasitic reference proteomes spanning six major eukaryotic lineages and two non-parasitic references. Protein sequences were analyzed using RIDAO and ESpritz, with disorder further evaluated using CH-CDF analysis. Gene Ontology enrichment was assessed using protti R package, and Pfam domain enrichment using eggNOG-mapper annotations. Predicted disorder was widespread but varied substantially among proteomes, consistent with differences in evolutionary lineage and organismal biology rather than a uniform association with parasitism. Predicted highly disordered proteins without LLPS propensity were enriched for DNA-binding and transcriptional regulatory domains, including zinc-finger, homeobox, and helix-loop-helix domains, whereas proteins with predicted LLPS propensity alone were enriched for Ras, WD40, proteasome, dynein, and ABC transporter domains. Proteins classified as both disordered and LLPS-prone showed significant enrichment of the RRM_1 RNA-binding domain in 13 of 15 proteomes, whereas Duffy-binding, PfEMP1, and EBA-175 domains were enriched only in P. falciparum. Exported P. falciparum proteins also had a higher median disorder fraction than non-exported proteins. These comparative computational analyses indicate that predicted intrinsic disorder and LLPS propensity are widespread but variable features of the analyzed proteomes. The results identify functional patterns and candidate proteins for further investigation, while highlighting the need for experimental studies to establish the roles of individual proteins in parasite biology, host interactions, and phase separation.

title: An image-based CRISPR screen reveals RNA processing control of HP1α condensates.
abstract: Heterochromatin protein 1α (HP1α) is a core component of heterochromatin, forming subnuclear condensates whose regulation and function remain poorly understood. Although RNA has been implicated in heterochromatin organization, how RNA influences HP1α localization remains unclear. Here, we develop an image-based CRISPR screening platform to systematically identify regulators of HP1α condensates and identify RNA processing as a central pathway. Perturbations that disrupt RNA processing increase HP1α-RNA interactions and reduce its association with chromatin, leading to loss of silencing. These findings establish RNA processing as a post-transcriptional mechanism that regulates HP1α localization and heterochromatin by altering the composition and nuclear distribution of HP1α-associated RNAs. More broadly, our work reveals functional crosstalk between RNA processing and chromatin organization, providing a framework for how RNA metabolism can influence nuclear architecture and gene regulation.

title: lncRNA XR_872037.3 functions as a ceRNA to promote cadmium-induced mice liver fibrosis by sponging miR-328-5p and activating the Alk7-TGF-β1/Smad pathway.
abstract: Cadmium (Cd), a toxic heavy metal environmental pollutant, can induce liver damage and promote hepatic fibrosis. Recent studies have revealed that the competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) mechanism regulates protein expression at the post-transcriptional level and influences hepatic fibrosis through multiple molecules or signaling pathways. However, few studies have elucidated the ceRNA-regulated network in Cd-induced liver fibrosis. In this study, we found through sequencing and PCR that lncRNA XR_872037.3 and Alk7 were highly expressed during cadmium-induced mouse liver fibrosis. Further investigation confirmed that silencing lncRNA XR_872037.3 alleviated fibrosis in mHSC cells and inhibited the Alk7-TGF-β1/Smad signaling pathway, and this effect could be reversed by inhibition of miR-328-5p. In summary, lncRNA XR_872037.3 acts as a ceRNA that competitively binds miR-328-5p to upregulate Alk7, thereby promoting Cd-induced hepatic fibrosis via the Alk7-TGF-β1/Smad signaling axis. These findings provide new insights into the biological effects of cadmium toxicity and its implications for environmental health research.

title: RNA Therapeutics in Cardiovascular Medicine: From Molecular Mechanisms to Clinical Practice.
abstract: RNA therapeutics are an exciting class of medications that target RNA and/or are themselves made from RNA. Most RNA therapeutics that have been approved for clinical use are antisense oligonucleotides or small interfering RNAs. To date, eight RNA therapeutics with cardiovascular relevance have received US Food and Drug Administration approval, but not all of them have specific indications for treating cardiovascular disease. There is a promising pipeline of additional cardiovascular RNA therapies targeting lipoprotein(a), angiopoietin-like protein 3, and angiotensinogen. Chemical modifications to therapeutic nucleic acids are important for conferring nuclease resistance and limiting immunostimulation in vivo, and enhanced delivery can be achieved using N-acetylgalactosamine conjugation and/or lipid nanoparticles. Emerging approaches include stereopure oligonucleotide chemistry, circular RNAs, adenosine-to-inosine RNA base editing, and nonhepatic targeting. This review summarizes the mechanistic basis of each modality, the clinical evidence for approved cardiovascular RNA therapeutics, selected pipeline candidates in advanced trials, and directions for future development.

title: Spaceflight is associated with mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation suppression and immune dysregulation that persist after return: a cross-mission transcriptomic analysis.
abstract: Human spaceflight exposes astronauts to microgravity and space radiation, yet whether these stressors produce a common molecular response across tissues has remained unclear. To address this, we performed a cross-mission meta-analysis of 70 spaceflight-versus-ground-control transcriptomic comparisons spanning 21 tissues and 16 missions from the NASA Open Science Data Repository, stratified by cumulative radiation exposure. We found that mitochondrial dysfunction is a consistent transcriptional signature of spaceflight: oxidative phosphorylation was significantly downregulated in the vast majority of in-flight datasets with exposure ≥10.34 mGy, accompanied by coordinated suppression of mitochondrial and cytosolic translation and mitochondrial protein import. In-flight datasets also showed activation of HIF-1α target genes and broad innate and adaptive immune dysregulation, including upregulation of mitochondrial DNA- and RNA-sensing transcripts consistent with mtDAMP-driven inflammation. After return to Earth, HIF-associated and most immune responses resolved, whereas oxidative phosphorylation suppression persisted in high-exposure datasets, dissociating transient adaptive responses from a sustained mitochondrial lesion. Mitochondrial suppression scaled with cumulative exposure and was greater in older, male, and C57BL/6 mice. Together, these findings establish mitochondrial dysfunction as a consistent, exposure-dependent, and persistent transcriptional feature to spaceflight, identifying mitochondrial bioenergetics and protein homeostasis as priority countermeasure targets for long-duration lunar and Mars missions. Biological insight We identify mitochondrial dysfunction as a conserved molecular response to spaceflight, characterized by suppression of oxidative phosphorylation, altered mitochondrial and cytosolic translation, and disruption of mitochondrial protein homeostasis. Technological innovation: We developed an integrated transcriptomic framework that harmonizes independent spaceflight datasets across missions, tissues, and biological backgrounds while preserving dataset-specific experimental structure. Benefit of integration: Joint analysis of 70 comparisons spanning 21 tissues and 16 missions revealed exposure-dependent and persistent mitochondrial alterations that were not apparent from individual datasets, while distinguishing sustained oxidative phosphorylation suppression from more transient stress and immune responses. This integrative approach provides a systems-level framework for identifying conserved biological responses and prioritizing mitochondrial pathways as potential targets for spaceflight countermeasures.

title: SUMOylation promotes polymerase stability by attenuating autophagic clearance in selected RNA viruses.
abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) play a key role in the evolutionary arms race between infectious bursal disease virus (IBDV) and its host. Understanding their effects on viral protein function and viral fitness may reveal antiviral targets. We investigated how small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) conjugation regulates VP1, the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp). Genetic and pharmacological perturbation of cellular SUMOylation linked VP1 SUMOylation status to efficient IBDV replication. VP1 SUMOylation was associated with greater VP1 stability, reduced polyubiquitination, and weaker association with the ubiquitin-binding autophagy receptor SQSTM1/p62 (sequestosome 1). K290R reduced polyubiquitination and partially restored the stability of VP1I404A, which showed markedly reduced SUMOylation; K290R also partially restored replication of recombinant IBDV carrying VP1I404T. These findings identify K290 as a key ubiquitination-associated residue without establishing it as the predominant ubiquitin acceptor site. Similar associations among SUMOylation status, polymerase abundance, ubiquitination, and SQSTM1 binding were observed in representative RdRps from the Birnaviridae and Flaviviridae families. Together, these findings support a role for SUMOylation in maintaining RdRp proteostasis and promoting efficient IBDV replication.

title: Engineering BHK-21 cells by dual knockout of host-restriction factors Cav1 and HDAC6 achieved a marked increase in FMDV titers for scalable vaccine production.
abstract: Foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV) vaccine production depends on BHK-21 cells, but the high antigen dose required for biannual mass vaccination campaigns using an inactivated vaccine limits global vaccine supply. In this study, a targeted small-molecule screen identified baicalein (caveolin-1 inhibitor) and tubacin (HDAC6 inhibitor) as potent enhancers of FMDV replication in BHK-21 cells. Cav1 was shown to act as an early restriction factor: its inhibition increased the viral entry and consequently produced a sixfold higher virus yield. Cav1 inhibition also primed p53-dependent intrinsic apoptosis, raising p53 phosphorylation and BAX/BIM transcripts, shifting cells into early apoptosis, and promoting cytolytic spread. HDAC6 was shown to function as a post-entry restriction factor: its inhibition elevated α-tubulin acetylation, enhancing viral RNA and protein expression and producing four to six times titer boost. Finally, using CRISPR/Cas9, we generated Cav1/HDAC6 double-knockout (dKO) BHK-21 cells, targeting two host restriction factors that impose entry and post-entry barriers to FMDV replication. The engineered BHK-21 cells in both adherent and suspension culture formats produced 10- to 20-fold higher virus titers across field FMDV serotype "O" and FMDV vaccine strains of serotypes "O," "A," and "Asia 1." Reintroducing either factor restored restriction, confirming their roles as host restriction factors. These findings reveal a dual-layer host defense mechanism and establish an engineered, high-yield BHK-21 cell line for enhanced viral production and improved vaccine manufacturing efficiency.IMPORTANCEFoot-and-mouth disease (FMD) imposes substantial economic losses on livestock-producing countries through reduced animal productivity and trade restrictions. Control relies on biannual herd vaccination, generating a demand for vaccine that often exceeds current manufacturing capacity. FMD vaccine antigen is conventionally produced in BHK-21 cells; however, limited viral yields increase production costs and constrain supply. Here, we identify caveolin-1 and HDAC6 as host restriction factors for foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV) in BHK-21 cells. Caveolin-1 restricts FMDV at the entry stage, whereas HDAC6 acts at a post-entry step. Knockout of these factors enhances viral yields by 10- to 20-fold across FMDV serotypes O, A, and Asia 1-the three serotypes included in India's trivalent vaccine program. These findings indicate that BHK-21 cells deficient in caveolin-1 and HDAC6 could substantially improve FMDV propagation and provide a scalable, cost-effective platform for vaccine manufacturing.

title: Effects of combining increased lysine (protein) supply and exogenous somatotropin on mammary development in late gestation gilt.
abstract: The goal of this project was to determine the impacts of increased dietary lysine (protein) and exogenous porcine somatotropin (pST) during late gestation, either separately or in combination, on mammary development of gilts. On day 85 of gestation, gilts were assigned to one of four groups: 1) fed SID lysine at estimated NRC requirement with daily injections of sterile water (CTL, control, n =17), 2) fed SID lysine at 40% above requirement via additional soybean meal and receiving daily injections of sterile water (LYS, n = 18), 3) fed SID lysine at estimated NRC requirement and receiving daily I.M. injections of 5 mg of pST (pST, n =19), or 4) fed SID Lys at 40% above requirement via additional soybean meal and receiving daily I.M. injections of 5 mg of pST (LYSpST, n = 17). The pST was diluted in 1 mL of sterile water. Dietary lysine treatment started on day 85 of gestation and pST treatment started on day 90 of gestation. The lysine treatment started earlier to maximize its potential effect, whereas the pST available did not allow for that. Both treatments lasted until slaughter on day 110, at which time mammary glands were collected and dissected. All gilts were weighed and had their backfat thickness measured at mating and on days 84 and 110 of gestation. Injections with pST increased mammary development leading to more parenchymal tissue (P < 0.001) that contained less percent fat (P < 0.0001), more percent protein, and greater concentrations of DNA and RNA (P < 0.0001), alongside increased alveolar expansion (P < 0.05). Supplementary lysine did not reproduce a previously-reported positive effect on mammary development. This divergence could be due to a lighter BW of gilts at the onset of treatment in the previous study, whereby supplementary lysine would have a beneficial effect only in lighter gilts. These data precluded any determination of whether combining supplementary dietary lysine and injections of pST in late-pregnant gilts act synergistically to enhance mammary development, whereas pST was effective in significantly improving both mammary parenchymal mass and composition.

title: METTL8 orchestrates TFH cell differentiation through m³C-mediated TCF1 regulation in infection and cancer models.
abstract: T follicular helper (TFH) cells are critical for humoral immunity against infections and correlate with immunotherapy efficacy, whereas immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy can drive their aberrant expansion, underscoring the need to understand the regulators controlling TFH cell fate. However, the epitranscriptomic regulation of their differentiation remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the 3-methylcytosine (m³C) methyltransferase METTL8 as a key regulator of TFH cell differentiation in both viral infection and cancer. METTL8 was preferentially expressed in CXCL13hi TFH cells, and its deficiency impaired TFH differentiation and germinal center responses in the lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus infection model and following anti-PD-1 immunotherapy in tumor models. Mechanistically, METTL8 exerted dual functions: it bound and stabilized Tcf7 mRNA through m³C modification, and it interacted with TCF1 protein to regulate chromatin accessibility and 3D genome organization at key TFH-associated loci, including Cxcr5 and Il6ra. Notably, ginkgolic acid treatment suppressed TFH responses without compromising the antitumor efficacy of anti-PD-1 therapy, an effect associated with METTL8. Collectively, our findings identify METTL8 as an epitranscriptomic regulator linked to RNA modification, TCF1-associated transcriptional control, and chromatin architecture during TFH differentiation and suggest that modulation of this pathway may provide a strategy to tune TFH-driven immune responses.

title: tsRNA-076 Promotes VSMC Autophagy and Vascular Remodeling by Activating IGF2BP2 Transcription.
abstract: tRNA-derived small RNAs (tsRNAs) are an emerging class of regulatory non-coding RNAs involved in diverse biological processes, yet their functions in the nucleus remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a nuclear-enriched tsRNA, tsRNA-076, that is markedly upregulated in synthetic vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) and plays an important role in vascular remodeling. Mechanistically, tsRNA-076 functions as an endogenous small activating RNA (saRNA) by directly associating with the IGF2BP2 (insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA binding protein 2) promoter and facilitating recruitment of the transcription factor ETV2 (ETS variant transcription factor 2), thereby driving transcriptional activation of IGF2BP2. Elevated IGF2BP2 enhances ATG5 expression by stabilizing its mRNA in an m6A-dependent manner, thereby promoting VSMC autophagy. Inhibition of tsRNA-076 attenuates VSMC autophagy and alleviates vascular remodeling in vitro and in vivo. Together, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized RNA activation mechanism mediated by tsRNA-076 and provide new insights into vascular remodeling.

title: RhoA upregulation in bronchial smooth muscle and its regulation by non-coding RNAs: a mechanistic basis for airway hyperresponsiveness in asthma.
abstract: Airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR) is a defining functional abnormality of bronchial asthma, and augmented contractility of bronchial smooth muscle (BSM) is one of its principal causes. Studies using a rat model of antigen-induced AHR first showed that the enhanced bronchoconstrictor response to acetylcholine could not be fully explained by voltage-dependent Ca2+ influx, but instead involved increased receptor-operated Ca2+ availability and upregulation of the heterotrimeric G protein Gq. Subsequent studies identified augmented agonist-induced Ca2+ sensitization of the contractile apparatus, mediated by the monomeric GTPase RhoA and its effector Rho-kinase (ROCK), as a further quantitatively important mechanism. The expression of RhoA protein was also found to be upregulated in hyperresponsive airways of both rats and mice. The Th2 cytokine interleukin-13 (IL-13), acting through signal transducer and activator of transcription 6 (STAT6), was later shown to directly upregulate RhoA in BSM cells and reproduce the contractile phenotype observed in disease models, whereas glucocorticoids were found to act, at least in part, by suppressing this RhoA upregulation. More recently, this upregulation has been linked to a non-coding RNA regulatory circuit: the microRNA miR-133a-3p normally represses RhoA translation and is downregulated in asthmatic BSM, whereas the long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) MALAT1 counteracts this repression by sponging miR-133a-3p and is itself upregulated in experimental asthma. This review traces this line of evidence, from the earliest description of enhanced Ca2+ handling in hyperresponsive airways, through the RhoA/ROCK Ca2+ sensitization pathway, to its upstream regulation by the IL-13/STAT6/MALAT1/miR-133a-3p axis, and considers the implications of this non-coding RNA network for future therapeutic strategies targeting AHR.

title: Neonatal sevoflurane exposures induced cognitive impairment via Satb2-mediated synaptic deficits.
abstract: Special AT-rich sequence-binding protein 2 (Satb2) is a DNA binding protein, and involved in transcription regulation and chromatin remodeling. Studies demonstrated that the absence of Satb2 mediated cognitive impairments in humans and rodents. Moreover, animal research reported that neonatal exposure to sevoflurane induced cognitive dysfunction in adolescent period, along with damage of synaptic plasticity, but the mechanisms are still not clear. Herein, we aimed to determine the role of Satb2 in neurotoxicity caused by sevoflurane. A total of 254 neonatal male Sprague-Dawley rats were used in this study. Neonatal rats were exposed to 30% O2 or 3.0% sevoflurane delivered in 30% O2 for 3 h on postnatal day 7 (P7). Cognitive function was evaluated through open field, Y maze, and novel object recognition tests from P28 to P35. The hippocampi were harvested on P14, P21, and P35. Effects of sevoflurane on Satb2, and synapse in the hippocampus were investigated by western blot, quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), and Golgi staining. To further screen key molecules, another batch of hippocampi were harvested immediately and 24 h after gas exposure, and subjected to RNA sequencing. Finally, Satb2 overexpression was induced by lentivirus injection into the lateral ventricle on P1, followed by gas exposure on P7. Next, some rats underwent behavioral tests on P28-P35. Hippocampi from another group of rats were harvested on P35 for Western blot, qRT-PCR, and Golgi staining. Y maze test showed that sevoflurane reduced the spontaneous alternation ratio in young rats. Novel object recognition test also revealed that sevoflurane decreased recognition index, the entries, and duration in novel arm, along with prolonged the latency to novel arm. Persistent decrease in Satb2, postsynaptic density protein-95 (PSD95), and spine density were observed. Moreover, RNA sequencing also revealed the decrease in Satb2 mRNA caused by neonatal exposure to sevoflurane. Furthermore, we found that lentivirus (LV)-induced Satb2 overexpression partially restored the decreases in the PSD95, spine density, spontaneous alternation ratio, recognition index, the entries, and duration in novel arm, and the increase in latency to novel arm caused by sevoflurane exposure. These results suggest that decreased Satb2 may contribute to cognitive disorders by reducing PSD95 levels, resulting in synaptic deficits. Meanwhile, this emphasizes that Satb2 was a potential target to intervening cognitive impairment caused by sevoflurane exposure.

title: Identification of Core Ferroptosis Regulatory Genes in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease Based on Single-Cell Transcriptomics and Multi-Cohort Machine Learning.
abstract: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) is one of the most common chronic liver diseases globally, yet its pathogenesis remains incompletely elucidated. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, has been demonstrated to play a crucial role in hepatocyte injury during MASLD and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis (MASH). However, the molecular mechanisms regulating the susceptibility of MASLD hepatocytes to ferroptosis remain unclear. Single-cell transcriptomics provides a novel perspective for resolving the heterogeneity of the hepatic microenvironment in MASLD, but there is still a lack of standardized pipelines for systematically identifying core ferroptosis-associated driver genes from massive single-cell datasets. This study performed an integrated analysis of six MASLD-associated snRNA-seq samples from GSE189600 (n=48,081 cells). Following dimensionality reduction, clustering, cell annotation, and ferroptosis scoring for each cell type, the hepatocyte subpopulation was extracted for high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA) to identify the M3 module, which was most highly correlated with MASH. Using the 108 cross-dataset consensus genes from this module as features, 101 two-stage machine learning algorithm combinations were trained on the GSE48452 cohort (n=73) and externally validated in two independent cohorts (GSE135251 and GSE89632). Global interpretation was conducted using fastshap (nsim=100 Monte Carlo) combined with shapviz to dissect core driver genes. Slingshot pseudotime analysis was utilized to track the dynamic changes of genes along the MASLD progression trajectory. CellChat analysis was applied to explore the cross-talk between the ferroptosis gene regulatory network and intercellular communication within the hepatic microenvironment. Virtual knockouts were performed using scTenifoldKnk to analyze downstream target-associated genes. Finally, the DrugReflector platform predicted drugs from the L1000 database, and molecular docking via AutoDock Vina was used to verify the drug accessibility of the core targets. Ferroptosis scoring revealed the ferroptosis susceptibility of MASLD hepatocytes. hdWGCNA identified the M3 module as the core MASH-associated module (r=0.60). The algorithm combination of glmBoost and random forest (randomForestSRC) demonstrated optimal performance (average AUC across 3 cohorts = 0.967). The fastshap SHAP analysis identified five core driver genes: ERBB2 (0.069), BACH1 (0.051), RBMS1 (0.050), NDRG2 (0.038), and CTSD (0.036). Pseudotime analysis showed that these five genes were temporally upregulated along the MASLD trajectory (Slingshot Lineage 2 correlation with MASH, r=0.702). BACH1 elevated first in early pseudotime, while ERBB2 and RBMS1 peaked in the intermediate phase. This study established a pipeline for identifying core MASLD regulatory genes, from single-cell transcriptomes to multi-cohort validation. A consistent SHAP importance ranking was validated through the glmBoost combined with random forest (randomForestSRC) algorithm and dual fastshap/kernelshap methods. This revealed that the five M3 module genes (ERBB2/BACH1/RBMS1/NDRG2/CTSD) constitute a multi-layered regulatory network for hepatocyte ferroptosis in MASLD, encompassing tyrosine kinase signaling (ERBB2), iron metabolism transcriptional regulation (BACH1), RNA-binding protein-mediated post-transcriptional regulation (RBMS1), metabolic stress adaptation (NDRG2), and lysosomal ferroptosis execution (CTSD). These five genes may serve as critical regulatory nodes and therapeutic targets for ferroptosis in MASLD.

title: IGF2BP2 stabilizes MSR1 and promotes malignant phenotypes and radioresistance in nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
abstract: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a common cancer type of head neck cancer, and its clinical treatment is affected by the acquired resistance such as radiotherapy resistance. Herein, the study intended to explore the involvement of insulin-like growth factor 2 (IGF2) mRNA binding proteins 2 (IGF2BP2) and macrophage scavenger receptor 1 (MSR1) in cancer progression and radiosensitivity of NPC. The mRNA detection was conducted via real-time quantification PCR and protein examination was performed by western blotting. Cell progression was assessed through cell counting kit-8 assay, colony formation assay, flow cytometry, wound healing assay and transwell assay. Radiosensitivity was evaluated by survival analysis and flow cytometry. RNA immunoprecipitation assay, m6A RNA immunoprecipitation (MeRIP), and dual-luciferase reporter assay were used to validate the interactions among METTL3, IGF2BP2 and MSR1. Xenograft models were established in mice to explore the role of IGF2BP2 in vivo. NPC tissues and cells expressed high level of MSR1. After MSR1 was silenced, NPC cell growth, migration and invasion were repressed while apoptosis was induced. Radiosensitivity of NPC cells was elevated by MSR1 knockdown. IGF2BP2 promoted the mRNA expression of MSR1 in an m6A-dependent manner, in coordination with the m6A methyltransferase METTL3. The effects of IGF2BP2 downregulation on cell development and radiosensitivity were abrogated with MSR1 overexpression. IGF2BP2 inhibition enhanced radiosensitivity of NPC tissues in mice. These findings uncovered the regulation of IGF2BP2 in the malignant development and radiation sensitivity in NPC by increasing MSR1 expression, providing the potential targets for NPC treatment.

title: Transforming nanotheranostics with machine learning: From nanostructure design to self-powered sensor and RNA theranostic applications.
abstract: Nanotheranostics, utilizing advanced nanomaterials for improved disease management, overcomes the shortcomings of conventional diagnostics and therapeutics. Notwithstanding significant technological progress, the implementation of nanotheranostic materials encounters impediments, e.g., protracted nanoparticle synthesis, insufficient comprehension of nano-bio interactions, and difficulties in the chemistry, manufacturing, and regulatory frameworks essential for clinical application and commercialization. Machine learning (ML), a crucial subset of artificial intelligence (AI), offers tools that help streamline the labour-intensive processes associated with nanotheranostic materials, potentially enabling its wider adoption. Here, this review surveys machine learning usage in nanoparticle synthesis, nano-bio interactions, diagnostics such as self-powered sensing, therapeutic strategies, and RNA theranostics. It discusses how machine learning enhances the design of biomolecular nanostructures, allowing stable functional platforms for precise assessment and targeted treatments. The review summarizes the challenges in the burgeoning domain of machine learning-assisted nanotheranostics and examines the future directions for creating next-generation nanotheranostics via the utilization of dependable datasets and powerful machine learning models to enhance clinical outcomes for patients.

title: Development and validation of potent, chemically stabilized, PARP1-selective siRNAs for in vivo gene silencing.
abstract: Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase 1 (PARP1) is a critical therapeutic target in various diseases due to its role in DNA repair and cellular homeostasis. While small molecule-based PARP inhibitors (PARPis) have shown promise as therapeutics, their efficacy is limited by off-target toxicity and resistance mechanisms. In this work, we developed potent, fully chemically stabilized small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) for selective PARP1 silencing. We screened a panel of 24 siRNA duplexes targeting PARP1 in human and mouse cell lines, identifying several potent candidates capable of achieving robust PARP1 knockdown across species. Lead siRNAs demonstrated high selectivity for PARP1 over PARP2, potent silencing at both the mRNA and protein levels, and biologic activity in multiple PARP1-dependent cellular models. In vivo mouse studies with docosanoic acid (DCA)-conjugated siRNAs showed significant P arp1 mRNA knockdown in liver, heart, and skeletal muscle following subcutaneous administration, reaching up to 80% knockdown under the conditions tested. Together, these results establish fully chemically stabilized PARP1-targeting siRNAs as potent and selective modulators of PARP1 expression in vitro and in vivo and support their further evaluation in oncology and other PARP1-associated diseases.

title: Curation and revision of gene models reveals unique features of helminth aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases.
abstract: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases (ARSs) play an essential role in protein synthesis by matching amino acids to their corresponding tRNAs. While antibacterial ARS inhibitors are in clinical use and anti-plasmodial compounds are in development, relatively little work has been done to develop inhibitors of ARSs in multicellular parasites, including helminths. Although more than 150 helminth genomes have now been sequenced, sequence predictions for ARSs and other proteins are often not completely correct. Inaccuracies, usually due to incorrectly predicted intron-exon boundaries, hinder identification of novel drug targets and development of a more complete understanding of helminth biology. Using publicly available genomic information from a set of twelve human-infecting helminths, we identified and corrected gene model predictions for ARS sequences. We corrected exon boundary predictions using available RNA-seq data, then refined and validated these predictions by comparison to existing robust multiple-sequence alignments of ARS homologs from other eukaryotes, bacteria, and archaea, resulting in new models for more than 50% of the sequences. Although most helminth ARS sequences have high similarity to human homologs, we found several unique features of helminth aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases that may be exploited to develop novel anthelminthic therapies. These include unusual mitochondrially-targeted ARSs that lack known RNA-binding domains and cytosolic ARSs in which appended domains, known to mediate assembly of the multi-aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase complex in humans and other metazoans, are missing or replaced with unique, helminth-specific sequences.

title: Extracellular Vesicles in Epilepsy: Molecular Mechanisms, Neuronal Signaling Pathways, and Biomarker Potential.
abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are membrane-bound vesicles secreted by cells (including neurons and glia). The biofluid profiles of EV-associated microRNAs, proteins, and glycans are not fixed but rather can change in response to the state of the releasing cells; moreover, the biofluid profile is dependent on the mixtures of cells and processing of the sample. Plasma EV-enriched microRNAs, coagulation factor IX and thrombospondin-1 in EV preparations from serum, and EV-associated N-glycan signatures have been reported to be candidates. Results from total serum, total CSF, brain tissue, and/or whole plasma validation are distinguished from EV-specific measurements. Activity-dependent EV release, activity-regulated cytoskeleton-associated protein (ARC)-mediated RNA transfer, and context-dependent effects on neuronal and glial signaling are supported by experimental studies. Circulating candidates are not proven to be brain-originating and/or causal. The majority of human results are left at the discovery or the initial validation, and estimations of discrimination do not prove clinical utility. Need for reproducible matrix-specific separation, assessment of non-EV contaminants and putative cellular enrichment, appropriate clinical comparators, and independent prospective validation.

title: Structure-Engineered Lipid-Mineral Nanoparticles for Ligand-Free Myeloid RNAi Delivery in Alzheimer's Disease.
abstract: Peripheral myeloid cells are key regulators of systemic inflammation and promising targets for immune intervention in Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, selective in vivo small interfering RNA (siRNA) delivery to these cells remains challenging because conventional lipid nanoparticles often exhibit predominant hepatic accumulation and usually require ligand or antibody modification for immune-cell targeting. Here, we report a structure-engineered lipid-mineral nanoparticle platform, termed MCP, for ligand-free myeloid RNA interference (RNAi) delivery. MCP integrates a calcium phosphate mineral phase with a phosphatidic acid-enriched lipid interface, enabling efficient siRNA incorporation. The Ca2+-lipid cooperative architecture promoted macropinocytosis-dependent uptake and preferential siRNA delivery to peripheral myeloid cells in vivo, particularly Ly6Chigh monocytes and macrophages, with enhanced delivery under AD-associated inflammatory conditions. Systemic delivery of MCP carrying siRNA against triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 1 (TREM1) attenuated neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative pathology in an AD mouse model, supporting peripheral myeloid reprogramming as a route to modulate central nervous system (CNS) disease progression. Notably, MCP also achieved efficient TREM1 silencing in AD patient-derived peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and restored TREM1 expression toward healthy-control levels. This work establishes a structure-driven, ligand-free lipid-mineral RNAi platform for peripheral immune intervention in AD.

title: Effects of Direct-Current Electric Field on Cellular Behaviors and Gene Expression in HTR-8/SVneo trophoblast cells.
abstract: Adequate invasion of trophoblasts into the uterus and decidua is essential for placental formation and fetal development. Endogenous electrotactic behavior has been observed in various cell types and electric fields (EFs) present during embryonic development. However, the response of trophoblasts to electric fields and the underlying mechanisms are unclear. This study investigated the effects of direct-current electric fields on trophoblasts behaviors. Cell images were recorded and analyzed using an image analyzer. Scratch wounds were created in confluent monolayers, and migration distances of wound edges were measured. Flow cytometry was used to analyze cell cycle progression and proliferation. Under the electric field, trophoblasts exhibited significant cathode-directed migration. Similarly, the cathode-facing edge of the scratch wound displayed a collective cathode-directed migratory response. EF exposure induced G2/M arrest and inhibited cell proliferation. Furthermore, the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified using RNA sequencing in EF-stimulated trophoblasts, which were verified by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Gene Ontology analysis revealed these DEGs were associated with biological processes including cell migration, proliferation, and cell cycle. Genome pathway analysis and protein-protein interaction analyses indicated significant enrichment of DEGs in the PI3K and MAPK signaling pathways. Western blotting confirmed the activation of AKT and ERK1/2 in trophoblasts exposed to EF. Inhibition of PI3K, AKT, or ERK1/2 attenuated the directional migration of trophoblasts and impaired the wound healing of scratch models under the electric field. Our results suggest direct-current electric fields regulate trophoblasts behaviors and transcriptome profiling provides novel insights into the mechanism of EF-guided cellular functions.

title: Regulation and Tumor-Promoting Functions of PD-L1 in Breast Cancer: Mechanisms, Tumor Microenvironment, and Therapeutic Implications.
abstract: Breast cancer is a heterogeneous malignant neoplastic disease of the breast that includes molecularly and clinically distinct subtypes with diverse biological characteristics, immune landscapes, and therapeutic responses. Programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) is expressed by malignant cells and by several immune-cell populations, and its abundance is shaped by genomic, epigenetic, transcriptional, RNA-level, and protein-level processes. Cytokine exposure, metabolism, hypoxia, and prior treatment further modify this checkpoint axis within the tumor microenvironment. Although PD-L1 is often detected in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), its frequency and clinical meaning depend on molecular subtype, cellular compartment, assay, and treatment setting. This narrative review brings together breast-cancer-specific findings on PD-L1 regulation, tumor-cell signaling, immune-cell interactions, biomarker performance, and combination treatment. Evidence generated directly in breast cancer is separated from mechanistic work in other tumor types, and the limits of such extrapolation are made explicit. We also examine why spatial and temporal heterogeneity, assay discordance, and treatment-related adaptation prevent PD-L1 from functioning as a stand-alone predictor in all clinical contexts.

title: Systems Biology and Machine Learning Reveal Oxidative Stress Hubs and Therapeutic Targets in Diarrhea-Predominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
abstract: Diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) is a common functional gastrointestinal disorder, and accumulating evidence suggests that oxidative stress is involved in its pathophysiology. This study explored oxidative stress-related mechanisms in IBS-D and screened potential diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets through integrative bioinformatics analysis. Transcriptomic datasets from the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI)-Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database were analyzed using integrative bioinformatics approaches to identify oxidative stress-related core genes in IBS-D. Eight potential biomarkers were identified and evaluated for diagnostic performance via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Among these, the key gene ACO2 was further investigated using Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG)-based gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and immune correlation analyses to explore the association between ACO2 expression and disease-related biological processes. In addition, the eight target proteins were used for reverse screening of potentially therapeutic traditional Chinese medicines and their active compounds. In total, 206 oxidative stress-related genes were identified, with predominant enrichment observed in mitochondrial energy metabolism and cellular stress-response pathways, including oxidative phosphorylation and hypoxia-inducible factor 1 (HIF-1) signaling. The eight potential diagnostic biomarkers demonstrated robust diagnostic performance (area under the ROC curve (AUC) = 0.896) in distinguishing IBS-D patients from healthy controls. Notably, ACO2 emerged as a key hub gene associated with distinct metabolic and immune-related pathway enrichment profiles. In parallel, a competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) regulatory network centered on ACO2 was established, providing additional insight into its potential post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms. Furthermore, reverse screening based on the eight target proteins identified luteolin, phillygenin, quercetin, and wogonin as candidate active compounds from Forsythia suspensa. Molecular docking further indicated favorable binding affinity between these compounds and the biomarker proteins. This integrative bioinformatics study identifies oxidative stress-related molecular signatures and potential biomarkers in IBS-D. Reverse screening and molecular docking further suggest that luteolin, phillygenin, quercetin, and wogonin from Forsythia suspensa may represent potential candidate compounds targeting these biomarkers. These findings provide a theoretical basis for further experimental validation.

title: Corneal epithelial signals remodel bacterial physiology and extracellular vesicle cargo in Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus epidermidis.
abstract: Host-microbe communication at the ocular surface is bidirectional, yet the reciprocal effects of corneal epithelial signals on bacterial physiology remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how corneal epithelial-derived exosomes and bacteria-epithelium co-culture influence Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a major opportunistic ocular pathogen, and Staphylococcus epidermidis, a common member of the ocular surface microbiota. Bacterial responses were assessed by transcriptomic and functional analyses, while bacterial extracellular vesicles released during epithelial interaction were characterized by proteomics and RNA sequencing. Corneal epithelial-derived exosomes reduced bacterial growth and increased epithelial adhesion in both species, while enhancing biofilm formation in P. aeruginosa. Bacteria-epithelium co-culture induced substantially broader responses than exposure to epithelial-derived exosomes alone. In P. aeruginosa, epithelial interaction reorganized quorum-sensing, motility, iron-acquisition, phenazine and biofilm-associated pathways, resulting in reduced motility and pyocyanin production, increased pyoverdine production and enhanced biofilm formation. In S. epidermidis, epithelial interaction was associated with reduced expression of several virulence factors associated with cytotoxicity and inflammatory responses, upregulation of genes associated with surface interaction and protein export, and decreased biofilm biomass. In both species, epithelial interaction also induced extensive remodeling of bacterial extracellular vesicle protein and RNA cargo, which did not simply mirror the corresponding intracellular bacterial profiles. These findings demonstrate that corneal epithelial signals actively drive species-specific bacterial adaptation and vesicular remodeling. Together with previous evidence of bacteria-to-epithelium signaling, they support a dynamic model of bidirectional interkingdom communication at the ocular surface.

title: Sex-specific alterations in gut microbiome composition in patients with Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: The microbiota-gut-brain axis plays a significant role in the pathology of Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, alterations in the gut microbiome structure of AD patients and the sex-specific differences in signature microbial taxa remain inadequately characterized. A total of 100 participants were enrolled, including 60 in the AD case group. Gut microbiota was analyzed by 16S ribosomal RNA (16S rRNA) sequencing. Models incorporating disease group, sex, and a disease-sex interaction term were constructed to test whether sex modifies the effect of AD on gut microbiota α diversity. Stratified analyses were performed to compare α and β diversity between the AD and healthy control (HC) groups in male and female populations, respectively. Differential signature taxa between the two groups were explored using linear discriminant analysis effect size (LEfSe) and random forest analysis. A total of 36,168 amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) were obtained, with 1,917 ASVs shared between the AD and HC groups. No interaction effect between AD and sex on gut microbiota diversity was observed (interaction p-FDR > 0.05). In the sex-stratified analysis, gut microbiota evenness indices (Simpson, Shannon, and Pielou's indices) were lower in AD patients than in controls among both male and female populations (p-FDR < 0.05), whereas species richness (Chao1 and Observed_species) was significantly reduced only in female AD patients (p-FDR < 0.05). Significant differences in gut microbiota beta diversity were observed between the AD and control groups in both the male population (Stress = 0.213) and the female population (Stress = 0.253) (ANOSIM; males: R = 0.365, p = 0.001; females: R = 0.133, p = 0.001). In the male population, 11 signature taxa, including Bacilli, Lactobacillales, and Macellibacteroides, were significantly enriched in the AD group; in the female population, 12 signature taxa, including [Ruminococcus], Alistipes, and Rikenellaceae, were significantly enriched in the AD group. In the overall prediction of the random forest model distinguishing the AD group from the control group, the accuracy was 85.71% and 90.77% in the male and female populations, respectively, and the taxa contributing most to group classification were Pseudoramibacter_Eubacterium and Lachnospira, respectively (Gini importance = 0.059 for both). The gut microbiota of AD patients exhibits distinct, sex-specific signature taxa.

title: Integrated multi-omics profiling identifies ECM-associated and systemic metabolic alterations associated with osteosarcoma metastasis.
abstract: Osteosarcoma metastasis remains a major clinical challenge, and the molecular programs underlying metastatic progression across omics layers are still incompletely understood. We established an orthotopic osteosarcoma metastasis model using fluorescence-labeled 143B cells and performed integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, and serum metabolomic profiling. Multi-omics integration identified cross-layer RNA-protein-metabolite associations and prioritized hub molecules, including COL1A2, SPARC, ATP1A2, ACTA1, and MPZ. Public validation in TARGET-OS and GSE21257 supported a conserved hub/ECM co-expression module across independent cohorts. Functional assays evaluated the role of COL1A2 in osteosarcoma cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. Histological examination confirmed lung metastatic lesions in 6/6 metastasis-bearing mice but not in non-metastatic controls. Transcriptomic and proteomic profiling revealed concurrent ECM remodeling and metabolic pathway alterations. Multi-omics integration identified 32 consistently altered molecules across all three omics layers. COL1A2 was prioritized as a key hub molecule. COL1A2 knockdown promoted, whereas COL1A2 overexpression suppressed, osteosarcoma cell proliferation, migration, and Transwell invasion. Rescue experiments confirmed COL1A2-dependent regulation of these malignant phenotypes. These findings reveal concurrent ECM remodeling and systemic metabolic alterations associated with osteosarcoma metastasis and identify COL1A2 as a functionally relevant ECM-associated hub molecule that may serve as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Engineering mRNA lipid nanoparticle for protein replacement in rare genetic diseases - current advances and future challenges.
abstract: Rare genetic diseases affect over 350 million patients worldwide and have long posed significant challenges in modern medicine. Although messenger RNA (mRNA) was initially considered unsuitable due to its instability, immunogenicity, and inability to cross biological barriers, the COVID-19 pandemic established mRNA as a clinically validated therapeutic. Advances in mRNA synthesis and lipid nanoparticle (LNP) design have since improved stability, translation, safety, and scalability, offering a modern strategy, alongside advances in our understanding of rare diseases. By enabling the production of functional proteins without modifying the genome, mRNA-LNP offer a flexible solution to restore proteins lost through rare genetic diseases. Despite this promise, their application for rare genetic diseases remains at early stages, with most candidates in preclinical developments or early Phase 1/2 trials. This review underlines recent advances in mRNA-based protein replacement for rare genetic disorders, integrating innovations in mRNA design combined with LNPs optimization. It also discusses current challenges, emerging innovations, and future perspectives. While early clinical programs have mainly targeted liver-based disorders, the field is expanding toward pulmonary, hematologic, and neuromuscular diseases. Continued multidisciplinary efforts may establish mRNA nanotherapies as a transformative treatment option for patients with rare genetic disorders.

title: Noncoding functions of FMR1 transcript in riboregulation of human neurodevelopment.
abstract: The noncoding functions of protein-coding messenger RNAs (mRNAs) are largely ignored. Here, we demonstrate an unexpected noncoding role of FMR1 mRNA in human neurodevelopment. A loss of FMR1 and its protein product, fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein (FMRP), leads to the neurodevelopmental disorder fragile X syndrome (FXS). Neurons derived from FXS patients display hyperexcitability and immature morphology, whereas FMRP knockout (FMRP-KO) neurons that retain FMR1 transcript expression do not. Multi-omics analyses reveal key metabolic differences between FXS and FMRP-KO neurons. Although both FXS and FMRP-KO neurons exhibit reduced mitochondrial respiration, only FXS neurons exhibit elevated glycolysis. We further discover that the FMR1 transcript riboregulates the levels of the glycolytic enzyme lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) by inhibiting the binding of LDHA mRNA to insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein 2 (IGF2BP2). Finally, the FMR1 transcript, independent of FMRP, rescues glycolytic and cellular deficits of FXS neurons. Together, these results suggest that FMR1 is a dual-function RNA in human neurodevelopment.

title: A Novel DHX9 Variant Was Identified in a Patient With Developmental Delay, Facial Dysmorphism and Seizure.
abstract: The DHX9 gene encodes an RNA helicase belonging to the DExD/H-box family, which is highly expressed in the brain and nervous system. Pathogenic variants in the DHX9 gene are associated with neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD) and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT). Both loss-of-function (LoF) and missense variants can cause NDD, whereas CMT is associated with specific missense variants. Patients with DHX9-related NDD typically present with intellectual disability, language and motor developmental delay, and autism spectrum disorder (ASD). CMT patients primarily present with distal weakness, sensory deficits, variable muscle wasting, foot deformities and painful sensory neuropathy. Here, we report a female patient with severe DHX9-related NDD phenotypes, including global developmental delay, ASD, facial dysmorphism, epilepsy, microcephaly, abnormal brain MRI findings and clinodactyly of the fifth finger. She experienced her first febrile seizure at 1 year and 2 months of age. She developed frequent myoclonic seizures characterized by rapid nodding and upper body tremors lasting 3-10 s at the age of 3 years. Simultaneous electroencephalogram (EEG) revealed paroxysmal bursts of high- to very-high-amplitude sharp-slow waves, spike-slow waves and polyspike-wave complexes diffusely over bilateral leads. Clinical exome sequencing (CES) identified a likely de novo missense variant in the DHX9 gene in the patient (NM_001357.5, c.1540C>T, p.(His514Tyr)). Notably, this variant resides within the highly conserved DEIH motif (Motif II) of the helicase ATP-binding domain. This critical region plays an essential role in ATP hydrolysis and helicase function.
