Three-dimensional protein structure modelling suggested that the p.(His514Tyr) substitution may compromise local protein stability by altering hydrogen bond networks. Our study expands the genetic and phenotypic spectrum of DHX9 variant-associated disorders.

title: mRNA‑Encoded Antibodies as a Powerful Arsenal Against Superbugs-Induced Sepsis.
abstract: Sepsis, a life-threatening organ dysfunction triggered by a dysregulated host response to infection, represents a formidable global health crisis, exacerbated by the relentless rise of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria. Antibiotic treatment is increasingly challenged by antimicrobial resistance, and conventional monoclonal antibody (mAb) therapies face significant manufacturing and logistical hurdles. This review focuses on the use of messenger RNA (mRNA) as a programmable platform to turn the patient's own body into a bioreactor for producing therapeutic antibodies on demand. We explore the transformative potential of this strategy, which merges the precision of antibody therapy with the speed and flexibility of nucleic acid technology. We critically analyze the ground-breaking preclinical evidence for mRNA-encoded antibodies against key bacterial virulence factors, such as the Pseudomonas aeruginosa Type III secretion system (T3SS). Beyond direct pathogen neutralization, we propose a visionary dual-pronged approach, combining anti-pathogen mRNA with immunomodulatory strategies to simultaneously control infection and rebalance the dangerously chaotic immune response characteristic of sepsis. However, the path to clinical reality is fraught with challenges, including targeted delivery to systemic infection sites, the dearth of long-term safety data, and the absence of a mature regulatory framework. We conclude by outlining a roadmap for the future, envisioning an era of multiplexed, personalized mRNA cocktails and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven design, which could finally provide a potent and adaptable weapon in the war against superbug sepsis and multi-organ failure.

title: ZDHHC20-Mediated Palmitoylation of METTL16 Represses the m6A-STEAP1 Axis and Confers Cell Resistance to Cuproptosis in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: Methyltransferase-like 16 (METTL16), an m6A methyltransferase, regulates metal metabolism, but its role in copper homeostasis and cuproptosis in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains unknown. Using ESCC cells exposed to CuCl2 or cuproptosis inducers, RNA interference, multi-omics, reader screening, and protein-turnover assays, we dissected the ZDHHC20-METTL16-STEAP1 axis. Xenograft and 4NQO-induced models, TCGA/GTEx datasets, and tissue microarrays were used for in vivo and prognostic analyses. Copper stress upregulated METTL16 and m6A modifications. METTL16 silencing reduced sensitivity to elesclomol-Cu/disulfiram-induced cuproptosis, which was rescued by STEAP1 overexpression. Mechanistically, METTL16 stabilized STEAP1 mRNA via m6A modification at position 286 with YTHDC1, enhancing cuproptosis sensitivity. Conversely, ZDHHC20 mediated METTL16 palmitoylation and cytoplasmic retention, suppressing STEAP1 stabilization and increasing cuproptosis resistance; ZDHHC20 depletion altered METTL16 localization without affecting its abundance or turnover. In vivo, ZDHHC20 knockout reduced esophageal lesion burden, whereas METTL16-IN-1 or vandortuzumab vedotin administration was associated with increased lesion burden in knockout mice. The VDM-associated observations did not establish STEAP1-specific inhibition in vivo. High ZDHHC20 correlated with poor prognosis, while elevated METTL16/STEAP1 predicted better survival. Targeting the ZDHHC20-METTL16-STEAP1 axis may overcome cuproptosis resistance in ESCC.

title: Recombinant AAV-Based Gene Therapy for Central Nervous System Disorders: From Gene Replacement to Precision Editing and Circuit Modulation.
abstract: Recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) vectors have moved central nervous system (CNS) gene therapy from experimental proof of concept to clinically validated treatment, yet therapeutic design remains highly dependent on disease mechanism, cellular distribution, and treatment timing. This narrative review examines recent progress in rAAV-based interventions for neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) and neurodegenerative disorders. For monogenic NDDs, gene replacement is most applicable to loss-of-function conditions with compatible payload size and tolerable expression, whereas dominant-negative, gain-of-function, and dosage-sensitive disorders may require allele-selective silencing or precise DNA or RNA editing. Rett syndrome illustrates both the reversibility of postnatal dysfunction and the need for tightly regulated transgene expression. Spinal muscular atrophy provides the leading translational paradigm: rAAV9-mediated SMN1 replacement demonstrates the value of early diagnosis, adequate tissue exposure, and treatment before irreversible neuronal loss. For complex neurodegenerative diseases, emerging strategies extend beyond simple gene addition. APOE-directed editing and protective-variant replacement may enable genotype-informed intervention in Alzheimer's disease, whereas Parkinson's disease programs combine restoration of dopamine synthesis, neuroprotection, and genetically encoded circuit modulation. Across these indications, major barriers include incomplete and nonselective CNS delivery, immune and dose-related toxicity, limited redosing, durable control of transgene or editor activity, off-target effects, and uncertain translation from animal models to humans. Progress over the next decade will depend on human-compatible vectors, cell-selective and regulatable expression, rigorous long-term safety assessment, biomarker-guided trials, and rational combinations that connect molecular target engagement to meaningful neurological benefit.

title: Nonreciprocal Hopfield nets for angiogenesis
abstract: During sprouting angiogenesis, endothelial cells dynamically reorganize among three relevant phenotypes (glycolytic, stalk and tip) to form new blood vessels, with cells transitioning from one phenotype to another. These cell-state transitions may involve intrinsic nonequilibrium dynamics that go beyond relaxation of the conventional Waddington landscape. We investigate this possibility using a nonreciprocal Hopfield network inferred from single-cell RNA sequencing and RNA velocity data for 1896 endothelial cells on a panel of 1873 genes. We encode the three experimentally identified phenotypes as correlated memory patterns and introduce an asymmetric mixing matrix describing their effective interactions. A dynamical mean- field reduction yields a three-dimensional system for the overlaps with these phenotypic memories, whose parameters are fitted to RNA-velocity-derived trajectories. The nonreciprocal model outperforms its reciprocal counterpart on held-out testing data. Remarkably, its long-time dynamics exhibit either stationary attractors or sustained cycles connecting phenotypic states, depending on the inference timescale. These results suggest that angiogenic cell fate decisions may involve directed, non-relaxational dynamics that cannot be captured by a conventional energy landscape. This approach may also provide a useful framework for investigating how perturbations constrain cellular differentiation.

title: Electrical stimulation promotes cardiomyocyte differentiation and cardiac development.
abstract: Electrical signals play critical roles in early heart development by regulating cardiomyocyte differentiation, proliferation, and energy metabolism. However, the mechanisms by which electrical stimulation (ES) influences early cardiac development remain incompletely understood. Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) and zebrafish embryos were employed as complementary in vitro and in vivo models. hiPSC-CMs were subjected to continuous ES from the cardiac mesoderm stage (day 4) to day 10 of differentiation. Cellular analyses included immunofluorescence, calcium imaging, proliferation assays, ATP quantification, and qRT-PCR. Zebrafish embryos were subjected to continuous ES for 10 h and 24 h post-fertilization (hpf), respectively. Subsequently, at 36, 48, and 72 hpf, the heart rate, contractile function, proliferation of cardiac cells, and vascular development were assessed. RNA sequencing was conducted on hiPSC-CMs and zebrafish embryos to assess transcriptomic changes, followed by bioinformatic pathway enrichment analysis. Functional studies involved siRNA mediated GATA4 knockdown in hiPSC-CMs, and in zebrafish embryos treated with a gata4 inhibitor, to systematically evaluate the effects of gata4 on cardiac function. ES significantly enhanced hiPSC-CMs differentiation, calcium handling, sarcomere maturation, proliferation, and energy metabolism, accompanied by upregulation of RYR2 and oxidative phosphorylation genes. In zebrafish embryos, ES accelerated body growth, yolk absorption, heart rate, cardiac contractility, and intersegmental vessel development. Transcriptomic analysis revealed upregulation of genes associated with sarcomere structure, calcium signaling, and energy metabolism, consistent with increased cardiac function and vascular development. Further investigation demonstrated that ES upregulated the expression of GATA4; GATA4 knockdown reduces hiPSC-CMs differentiation, while its inhibitor 3i 1000 abolishes ES enhanced zebrafish heart contractility. These findings indicate that GATA4 plays a significant role in the regulation of cardiac differentiation and heart development by ES. ES promotes early cardiac cell differentiation and cardiovascular development by enhancing energy metabolism, associated with increased GATA4 related transcriptional activity. These findings offer mechanistic insights into bioelectrical cardiac development, laying a foundation for regenerative therapies for congenital and early-stage heart diseases.

title: SAMHD1 functions as a repressor of LINE-1 retrotransposons in human germ cell development.
abstract: Long interspersed element 1 (LINE-1 [L1]) retrotransposons constitute at least 17% of the human genome and threaten genomic integrity because of their autonomous retrotransposition activity. Sterile alpha motif (SAM) domain and HD domain-containing protein 1 (SAMHD1) inhibits the formation of retroviruses, DNA viruses, and L1 elements. However, the role of SAMHD1 in regulating L1 retrotransposition during human germline development remains largely unknown. Here, we report that methyltransferase-like 3 (METTL3) depletion in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) upregulates SAMHD1 expression, while concurrently, L1 retrotransposons are elevated during in vitro induction of spermatogonial stem cell-like cells (hSSCLCs) from these hESCs. RNA-seq analysis revealed that the upregulated genes were enriched in autophagy and the defense response to viral processes. Knockdown of SAMHD1 significantly impaired the in vitro differentiation efficiency of hSSCLCs. Mechanistically, SAMHD1 promoted L1 retrotransposon degradation via autophagy, which was associated with increased phosphorylation of eukaryotic initiation factor 2 alpha (eIF2α). Additionally, the reverse transcription inhibitor d4t abolished L1 retrotransposition caused by downregulating SAMHD1 expression. Analysis of human fetal testis samples, which exhibited high levels of L1 transcripts, revealed that SAMHD1 localized to both the nucleus and the cytoplasm, as determined by costaining with the germ cell marker Vasa homolog (VASA; also known as DEAD-box helicase 4 [DDX4]). Analysis of adult human testis samples confirmed SAMHD1 expression in spermatogonial stem cells. Our findings suggest that SAMHD1 may act as a guardian of genome stability during human germline development and provide novel insights into its function and regulatory mechanisms in restricting L1 retrotransposition.

title: Isolation and characterization of human thymic epithelial cells.
abstract: The human thymus is critical for establishing a functional adaptive immune system, with reduced cancer risk, increased healthy aging, and longevity all linked to its function. However, the molecular and physiological mechanisms of these associations are incompletely understood. For the reproducible identification of mechanisms and mitigating cell types, consistent tissue processing and analysis techniques are essential. Here, we assessed biological and technical parameters for the processing, isolation, and analyses of human thymic epithelial cells (TECs). We found that EpCAM and autofluorescence emissions in the range of 500 to 650 nm excited by the 405 nm laser are sufficient to distinguish TECs from other thymic cells, particularly the autofluorescent population. We identified CD205 as the target of the classical cortical TEC antibody CDR2 and re-established CD205 as a reliable marker to distinguish cortical and medullary TECs, which we confirmed by single-cell RNA sequencing. In a systematic comparison of sample processing and digestion conditions, we assessed representative tissue sample size and protein staining patterns, which enabled us to clarify and reconcile inconsistencies across previously published results. Lastly, we established a minimal flow cytometry panel sequencing for the isolation of major TEC populations and their developmental stages. In summary, we provide recommendations to improve reproducibility in the study of human TEC biology and thymus function.

title: Immune-stimulatory cytokine IL-18 induces inflammatory senescence and impairs stem cell-mediated experimental skeletal regeneration.
abstract: Stem cell-based therapies offer potential for repairing large skeletal defects, yet persistent inflammation limits their efficacy. Here, we identify macrophage-derived IL-18 as an immune switch that impairs skeletal regeneration by disrupting immune-mesenchymal cell interactions. IL-18 is elevated in male mouse non-healing models and human bone nonunion samples, supporting its translational relevance. Mechanistically, IL-18 acts as an upstream amplifier of inflammation by inducing Serpina3f transcription, thereby driving macrophage senescence and M1 polarization and triggering a feed-forward inflammatory cascade that suppresses mesenchymal stem/stromal cell osteogenesis. Single-cell RNA sequencing and functional assays further show that IL-18 directly impairs mesenchymal stem/stromal cell proliferation, clonogenicity, and mitochondrial fitness. Genetic deletion of IL-18 restores regenerative potential, whereas pharmacological blockade with IL-18-neutralizing antibodies or IL-18 binding protein reverses macrophage dysfunction and promotes bone healing. These findings establish IL-18 as a key mediator of inflammation-induced regenerative failure and a potential therapeutic target for skeletal regeneration.

title: Nanozyme-Catalyzed Lateral Flow Assay for the Simultaneous Detection of RNA and Protein Biomarkers.
abstract: Molecular diagnostics have advanced rapidly over the past decade, driven by the demand for accessible and scalable testing solutions. However, current assays often focus on single biomolecule types, limiting their ability to capture the multifactorial nature of disease. Integrating distinct molecular readouts─such as transcriptomic and proteomic biomarkers─could provide richer diagnostic information and improve clinical decision-making. Here, we present MOSAIC (Multiplexed Orthogonal Sensing Assay Integrated with CRISPRZyme), a unified lateral flow assay that enables simultaneous detection of RNA and protein biomarkers using a shared nanozyme-catalyzed readout. The assay combines CRISPR/Cas13a-mediated RNA detection and antibody-based protein detection, with assay components optimized through antibody conjugation tuning, blocking agent optimization, and probe loading calibration to achieve balanced and cross-talk-free performance. Using cardiovascular disease as a model, the platform successfully detects NTproBNP and LIPCAR long noncoding RNA simultaneously from the same sample. The assay was further optimized for spiked human plasma, incorporating tailored pretreatment and recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) to maintain RNA stability and performance in complex biofluids. Extending its versatility, the same assay design was adapted to detect SARS-CoV-2 biomarkers, the spike (S) protein and ORF1ab gene, in pooled human saliva. To enable standardized interpretation of multiplexed readouts, we additionally developed a machine-learning-assisted computational workflow that automates strip localization, signal extraction, and calibration curve construction. Together, these results demonstrate a modular, paper-based diagnostic platform that unites transcriptomic and proteomic analyses within one assay architecture, offering a practical step toward accessible and multiplexed molecular diagnostics across diverse disease contexts.

title: Targeting CDK7/9 and casein kinase 1 alpha as a therapeutic strategy in advanced-stage uveal melanoma.
abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM) patients frequently develop advanced-stage disease in the liver, but treatment options are limited. The low tumor mutation burden and the transcriptional rewiring observed in aggressive, BRCA1-associated protein 1 (BAP1)-deficient UM led us to investigate transcriptional-based inhibitors in preclinical models. Drug screening data and analysis of the Dependency Map (DepMap) indicated that UM cell lines exhibit a strong dependency on the transcriptional cyclin-dependent kinases, 7 and 9 (CDK7/9). Treatment of BAP1-deficient UM cell lines with SY-5609, a CDK7 inhibitor, led to growth inhibition associated with stalled cell cycle progression. Casein kinase 1 alpha (CK1α) is highly expressed in BAP1-deficient UM patient tumors and treatment of BAP1-deficient UM cell lines with A51, a CDK7/9 plus CK1α inhibitor led to both cell cycle arrest and induction of cell death. RNA-sequencing and protein array analysis associated A51 effects with down-regulation of the pro-survival protein, MCL1. Depletion of MCL1 enhanced cell death in SY-5609-treated UM cells, whereas overexpression of MCL1 rescued cell death in A51-treated UM cells. In a non-invasive in vivo liver injection model of UM tumor growth, A51 reduced tumor onset and improved overall survival. Overall, these studies show that A51 causes cell death in advanced-stage UM preclinical models, at least in part, through down-regulating MCL1.

title: Integrative transcriptomic and machine learning analyses identify NOL7 and TXLNA as candidate blood biomarkers for Parkinson's disease within an RNA modification-associated co-expression network.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) pathogenesis involves complex molecular mechanisms, with emerging evidence implicating RNA modifications (RM). This study sought to explore RM-associated key genes and their roles in PD progression. Transcriptomic datasets GSE6613 (training) and GSE72267 (validation) were analyzed. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between PD and controls were recognized. WGCNA was performed to identify RM-associated module genes. Machine learning algorithms, Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis, and gene expression validation were applied to screen key genes. Nomogram construction, functional enrichment, immune infiltration analysis were conducted to investigate the biological mechanisms and therapeutic potential of the key genes. The bioinformatics findings were further supported by RT-qPCR experiments in a small clinical cohort (n = 5 per group), though these preliminary results require validation in larger independent samples. Through intersection of 507 DEGs and 2,091 RM-associated module genes, 63 candidate genes related to RM in PD were identified. Machine learning, ROC analysis, gene expression validation, and clinical experiments were further employed to identify two key genes (NOL7 and TXLNA). A nomogram constructed based on key genes demonstrated moderate diagnostic efficacy for PD, with an area under the curve of 0.792. Enrichment analyses revealed associations of the key genes with neuroactive pathways, such as spliceosome and ribosome. Immune infiltration analysis suggested a negative correlation between NOL7 and NKT (cor = -0.30, P < 0.05). Furthermore, danazol was predicted to be a compound associated with both NOL7 and TXLNA. Molecular docking analysis revealed that danazol exhibited a relatively favorable binding affinity for NOL7 (-6.3 kcal/mol), whereas its binding affinity for TXLNA was weaker (-4.7 kcal/mol). NOL7 and TXLNA were validated as blood biomarkers for PD derived from an RNA modification-associated transcriptional module, offering insights into epigenetic dysregulation and immune interactions. The nomogram provided a preliminary framework for PD risk assessment, and the drug prediction offered potential candidates for future therapeutic exploration.

title: Predictive modeling of single-cell transcriptomic dynamics with Dynamo.
abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) provides a powerful means to investigate cell fate dynamics during development and disease. However, existing computational approaches-such as RNA velocity-are often limited to qualitative and descriptive insights. We previously presented Dynamo, a machine learning framework that leverages noisy RNA velocity estimates to learn analytical and predictive vector fields of gene expression dynamics. These learned vector fields enable a suite of novel, quantitative analyses, including mapping the geometry of cell state transitions, identifying dynamic features of differentiation trajectories, inferring gene regulatory networks, predicting optimal paths and transcription factor cocktails for cellular reprogramming, and simulating in silico genetic perturbations. Here we provide a comprehensive protocol for applying Dynamo across four distinct data types and five downstream analyses, demonstrating its versatility in handling conventional and metabolic-labeling-enabled scRNA-seq, multiomic datasets and even datasets without velocity information. We also show that Dynamo can predict cell fate diversions following genetic perturbations and accurately identify key transcription factors that enable lineage transitions in the hematopoietic system. By enabling predictive modeling from single-cell data, our protocol aims to empower the development of generative and predictive models of single-cell genomics. While typical RNA velocity vector field analyses can be completed in less than an hour, the nine case studies in the Protocol can be completed in ~7 h and 35 min. The Protocol is designed for researchers with basic familiarity in scRNA-seq analysis and Python programming, although no advanced coding expertise is required.

title: Development of a diagnostic biomarker panel for early-stage lung adenocarcinoma using serum-derived small RNAs.
abstract: Circulating small RNAs, such as microRNAs (miRNAs) and transfer RNA fragments (tRFs), reportedly reflect the physiological and pathological conditions in various diseases. Herein, we aimed to identify circulating small RNAs for the early diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma. This study included 40 healthy controls and 43 patients with lung adenocarcinoma. We analyzed their serum using small RNA sequencing and identified differentially expressed small RNAs between healthy controls and patients with lung adenocarcinoma. We verified the expression profiles of these small RNAs in 29 patients with lung adenocarcinoma and 27 healthy controls. Finally, we evaluated our current results by performing machine learning-based analysis. The expressions of two mature miRNAs (miR-193a-5p, miR-423-5p), one miRNA isoform (isomiR) (miR-423-5p(21nt)), and two tRFs (tRF-Gly(CCC)(29nt), tRF-Gly(CCC)(30nt)) were significantly elevated in patients with lung adenocarcinoma than in healthy controls. Moreover, the expressions of one miRNA (miR-20a-5p) and five tRFs (tRF-iMet(CAT)(31nt), tRF-Lys(CTT), tRF-iMet(CAT)(30nt), tRF-iMet(CAT)(29nt), tRF-Val(AAC)) were significantly decreased in patients with lung adenocarcinoma than in healthy controls (area under the curve [AUC] values = 0.71 to 0.85, respectively). Furthermore, a combination of six small RNAs (miR-193a-5p, miR-423-5p(21nt), miR-20a-5p, tRF-Gly(CCC)(29nt), tRF-iMet(CAT)(29nt), and tRF-Val(AAC)) was useful for developing a biomarker panel for the early diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma. Discovery screening revealed that the panel demonstrated a sensitivity of 0.954 and a specificity of 0.925 (AUC = 0.974), whereas the validation data demonstrated a sensitivity of 0.690 and a specificity of 0.926 (AUC = 0.924). Serum-derived small RNAs are associated with the status of patients with lung adenocarcinoma, and evaluating small RNAs in serum is a promising non-invasive approach for diagnosing lung adenocarcinoma at an early stage.

title: Severe hyperchylomicronemia sensitizes the heart to pathological remodeling: evidence from GPIHBP1-deficient mice.
abstract: Circulating triglyceride and triglyceride-rich lipoprotein (TRL) accumulation is increasingly recognized as a residual atherosclerotic risk, but their specific effects on cardiac remodeling and heart failure (HF) remain largely unexplored. Here, this issue was investigated in Gpihbp1 knockout (KO) mice, which develop severe hyperchylomicronemia due to disruption of intravascular TRL hydrolysis. Cardiac lipid metabolism and remodeling were evaluated in 10-month-old Gpihbp1 KO mice and their wild-type littermates under physiological conditions. Mice were also subjected to transverse aortic constriction (TAC) to evaluate the effects of severe hyperchylomicronemia on pressure overload-induced remodeling and HF. Furthermore, Gpihbp1 KO mice were crossed into an low-density lipoprotein receptor (Ldlr) KO background to study the effects of severe hyperchylomicronemia on hemorheology and high-fat diet (HFD)-induced cardiac pathology. Untargeted cardiac lipidomics revealed 214 differentially regulated lipid species that were specifically enriched in glycerophospholipid, fatty acid (FA) and diacylglycerol subclasses. Quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) confirmed that FA oxidation-related genes were downregulated and that glucose utilization-related genes were upregulated. Electron microscopy revealed swollen mitochondria with fragmented cristae, and RNA-seq revealed reduced respiratory chain gene expression. These abnormalities resulted in impaired cardiac contractile performance in 10-month-old Gpihbp1 KO mice without the induction of hypertrophy or fibrosis. After TAC, Gpihbp1 KO hearts exhibited exaggerated diastolic dysfunction and more severe myocyte hypertrophy and fibrosis. In Gpihbp1/Ldlr double-knockout (dKO) mice, reduced erythrocyte deformability and increased whole blood viscosity were observed and worsened post-HFD. Additionally, HFD consumption resulted in significant diastolic impairment, cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis in dKO mice. Severe hyperchylomicronemia due to Glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored high-density lipoprotein-binding protein 1 (GPIHBP1) deficiency sensitizes the heart to pathological remodeling and HF. These findings indicate a potential pathogenic contribution of hypertriglyceridemia and TRL accumulation to cardiac disease.

title: Multiplex immunohistochemistry in multiple myeloma: principles, spatial profiling applications, and emerging frontiers in immuno-oncology.
abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) progression and therapeutic resistance are dictated by the bone marrow microenvironment (BMME). Conventional single-marker immunohistochemistry (IHC) cannot resolve the complex cellular neighborhoods, non-cellular signaling networks, and spatial exclusion patterns that characterize this disease. Multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC) and allied high-plex spatial imaging technologies now enable simultaneous visualization of 6 to over 60 protein targets on a single formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) section while preserving tissue architecture. This review first establishes a rigorous technical foundation by reclassifying mIHC and related high-dimensional imaging platforms according to their detection readout modality-fluorescence spectral unmixing/tyramide signal amplification (TSA) cyclic staining, DNA-barcode cyclic hybridization, metal-isotope mass spectrometric imaging, and regional-photolysis digital spatial profiling-and by clarifying several long-standing technical misconceptions (e.g., the historical relationship between PhenoCycler and Vectra Polaris, the cyclic nature of the Opal/TSA workflow, and the true elution chemistry of CODEX and t-CyCIF). We then present an expanded, bone-marrow-specific horizontal comparison of mIHC against flow cytometry, mass cytometry (CyTOF), imaging mass cytometry (IMC)/multiplexed ion beam imaging (MIBI), and spatial transcriptomics. Building on this technical scaffold, we organize the biological and clinical applications of mIHC along the natural disease continuum-monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) → smoldering myeloma (SMM) → newly diagnosed MM (NDMM) → post-treatment residual disease → relapsed/refractory MM (RRMM) → extramedullary disease (EMD)-integrating T-cell, stromal, myeloid, and NK-cell compartments together with cytokine networks, metabolic competition, and bone-remodeling signals. We further delineate realized multimodal integration paradigms (mIHC combined with spatial transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, digital spatial profiling, and artificial intelligence) and, separately, the technical, economic, and workflow bottlenecks-including spectral overlap, antibody cross-reactivity, turnaround time, cost, and the choice between bone marrow clot and decalcified trephine specimens-that currently constrain clinical translation. As methodological workflows for decalcified bone marrow specimens mature, mIHC is transitioning from a research tool to a critical component of precision immuno-oncology, offering actionable insights for overcoming CAR-T resistance and improving risk stratification.

title: [Role of Pathogenic Microorganisms in the Prognosis of Chronic Wounds].
abstract: To investigate the relationship between patient outcomes and biofilms in chronic wound infections, and to analyze the effects of microbial diversity and population dynamics on wound prognosis at different stages of chronic wound formation. We enrolled 104 patients with wound infections from West China Hospital, Sichuan University. According to the wound type, patients were divided into a trauma group (n = 56) and an ulcer group (n = 48). Based on treatment outcomes, patients were also divided into an improvement group (n = 14) and a deterioration group (n = 73). Microbial diversity analysis of wound biofilms was performed using conventional clinical microbial culture combined with matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry and 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene amplicon sequencing. The sequencing results were analyzed using bioinformatics techniques, including amplicon sequence variant (ASV) analysis and differential species analysis. A total of 185 pathogen isolates, comprising 76 different species, were obtained from all wound samples using conventional microbial culture. A total of 33511 ASVs were identified by 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. Among these, 22791 ASVs were unique to the improvement group, 5365 ASVs were unique to the deterioration group, and 5355 ASVs were shared by both groups. The abundance of Klebsiella, Providencia, Stenotrophomonas, and Streptococcus were significantly higher in the improvement group than that in the deterioration group, while the abundance of Finegoldia, Peptoniphilus, Porphyromonas, and Prevotella were significantly higher in the deterioration group than that in the improvement group. Analysis of the trauma and ulcer groups across phylum, class, order, family, genus, and species levels using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing revealed greater differences between the two groups in the pathogens identified at the species level. Predominant species in the trauma group included Anaerococcus vaginalis, Porphyromonas asaccharolytica, and Prevotella buccalis, while the ulcer group mainly featured Corynebacterium auriscanis, Corynebacterium striatum, and Anaerococcus vaginalis. 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing provides complementary information to traditional identification methods. Differences in the composition of microbial communities in biofilms may be closely associated with the formation of chronic wounds. Differences in microbial structure, variations in abundance, and differences in functional genes within biofilms may have important effects on wound outcomes.
extra: Sichuan Da Xue Xue Bao Yi Xue Ban

title: A pH/ROS-responsive TWIST1-targeting nanogel for epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity modulation and combination immunotherapy in lung cancer.
abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has substantially improved outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), although durable responses remain limited in a large fraction of patients. Increasing evidence links this resistance to epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), a cellular program that not only enhances invasiveness but also restricts T-cell access within the tumor microenvironment. By integrating transcriptomic profiles from immunotherapy-resistant lung cancer organoids with The Cancer Genome Atlas Lung Adenocarcinoma cohort (TCGA-LUAD) and independent immunotherapy datasets, we identified twist family bHLH transcription factor 1 (TWIST1) as a central epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-associated factor linked to poor immunotherapeutic response. Tumors with high TWIST1 expression displayed reduced CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, attenuated cytotoxic immune signatures, and unfavorable clinical outcomes. To interfere with this EMT-associated immune resistance, we developed oxidized hyaluronic acid/oxidized dextran-thioketal nanogels (OO-TK NGs) for the localized delivery of small interfering RNA targeting TWIST1 (siTWIST1), termed siTWIST1@OO-TK NGs. The nanogel was constructed from oxidized hyaluronic acid and oxidized dextran, crosslinked through a thioketal-containing bis-hydrazide linker that undergoes degradation under acidic and reactive oxygen species (ROS)-rich tumor-mimic conditions. This design enabled controlled intracellular release of siTWIST1 in tumor cells. TWIST1 silencing restored E-cadherin expression while reducing Vimentin and matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP9) levels, accompanied by diminished proliferation, and migration. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) tumor-bearing mice. Administration of siTWIST1@OO-TK NGs suppressed intratumoral TWIST1 expression, delayed tumor progression, and extended survival. The effect became more pronounced when combined with programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) blockade treatment, which increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration and enhanced IFN-γ-related effector activity within tumors. In a lung metastasis model, combination therapy markedly reduced metastatic burden and MMP9 expression, consistent with partial reversal of the EMT-associated markers. These findings support the potential of combining microenvironment-responsive TWIST1-targeted siRNA delivery with PD-1 blockade to concurrently modulate tumor plasticity and antitumor immunity. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Immune checkpoint blockade has reshaped the treatment landscape of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet resistance remains a major clinical obstacle. Increasing evidence suggests that epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) contributes to this resistance by establishing an immune-excluded tumor microenvironment that limits cytotoxic T-cell infiltration and function. In this study, through integrated analyses of immunotherapy-resistant organoid transcriptomes and clinical datasets, we identify TWIST1 as a key regulator linking EMT activation to impaired antitumor immunity and poor response to PD-1 blockade. Based on these findings, we developed a dual-responsive hydrogel nanogel system for tumor-selective delivery of siTWIST1. The nanogel undergoes degradation under acidic and reactive oxygen species-rich conditions characteristic of the tumor microenvironment, enabling controlled intracellular release of siRNA. TWIST1 silencing reversed EMT-associated phenotypes, suppressed tumor invasion and metastasis, and substantially enhanced the therapeutic efficacy of anti-PD-1 treatment in vivo through increased CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration and restoration of IFN-γ-associated immune activity.

title: A spatiotemporal atlas of maturation and aging of the male monkey hypothalamic-pituitary-testicular axis.
abstract: Reproductive maturation in males is achieved only after puberty through the functional integration of the hypothalamic-pituitary-testicular (HPT) axis. However, the molecular programs that coordinate this multi-organ transition remain largely undefined. Here, we generated a spatiotemporal atlas of the cynomolgus monkey HPT axis across juvenile, pubertal, adult, and old stages using spatial ATAC-RNA sequencing together with single-nucleus and single-cell RNA-sequencing. This atlas delineates stage-associated transcriptional, chromatin, and spatial changes in HPT axis-relevant populations, including KNDy neurons, gonadotropes, Sertoli, and Leydig cells. KNDy neurons exhibit transitions between quiescent-like and excitatory-like transcriptional states and display spatial reorganization with astrocytes that may correlate with HPT-axis maturation. During aging, the hypothalamus and testis display senescence-associated changes, whereas the pituitary exhibits shared age-associated transcriptional changes across endocrine populations and reduced organizational structure entropy. Our spatiotemporal atlas thus provides a valuable resource for investigating the molecular mechanisms underlying HPT-axis maturation, aging, and related diseases.

title: CosMxScope: scalable reconstruction and digital pathology integration of imaging-based CosMx spatial transcriptomics data.
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics technologies have transformed the capacity to quantify gene expression from human tissues, simultaneously capturing both the cell functional state and spatial organization at cellular and subcellular resolution. The CosMx Spatial Molecular Imager (SMI) is one of the leading platforms at single-cell spatial multi-modal omics profiling, capable of measuring thousands of RNA or protein targets at single-cell and subcellular resolution across whole slide sections. Exported data include field-of-view (FOV) image tiles, subcellular transcript coordinates, and cell segmentation polygons, outputs that are rich in spatial information but not directly compatible with widely used digital pathology tools. Here we present CosMxScope, a lightweight open-source Python framework designed for data exported from the CosMx Spatial Molecular Imager through the AtoMx platform, bridging CosMx spatial outputs with histopathology visualization environments. CosMxScope provides functions for stitching FOV image tiles into reconstructed whole-slide images, converting cell segmentation polygons and transcript coordinates into GeoJSON objects for downstream visualization and assessment within QuPath, and generating spatial visualization plots of cell types, transcript locations, and gene expression patterns. The framework is designed for practical use in translational research settings, enabling interactive exploration of spatial transcriptomic data alongside cell morphology. CosMxScope has been applied in multiple ongoing research projects involving CosMx profiling of human and mouse tissues, supporting pathology-based spatial analysis workflows. This open-source software is available at https://github.com/AivaraX-AI/CosMxScope.

title: CD22 and CD79A expression level in bladder cancer patients using bioinformatics tools, RNA-Seq and qRT-PCR validation.
abstract: Bladder cancer is a prevalent malignancy with high morbidity and mortality, necessitating the identification of novel biomarkers for improved diagnosis and treatment. CD22 and CD79A, traditionally recognized as B-cell surface markers, have emerged as genes of interest due to their roles in the tumor microenvironment and potential as immune markers and therapeutic targets. Raw RNA-Seq data from the GSE133624 dataset were processed and analyzed using the Galaxy web server. The bioinformatics pipeline incorporated multiple tools, including HISAT2, featureCounts, and DESeq2 to identify genes with significant expression changes. CD22, CD79A, TCL1A, and VPREB3 were selected through STRING- and Cytoscape-based protein-protein interaction analysis with biological support. For validation, total RNA was isolated from peripheral blood of 27 patients and 25 healthy controls using TRIzol reagent. Complementary DNA (cDNA) was synthesized, and gene expression was measured by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). Bioinformatics analysis revealed significant downregulation of CD22 (log2FoldChange: -3.30, adjusted P = 2.49 × 10⁻10) and CD79A (log2FoldChange: -2.54, adjusted P = 1.13 × 10⁻5) in tumor tissues, with roles in immune and signaling pathways. qRT-PCR showed no significant expression differences in blood (P = 0.2361 for CD22, P = 0.531 for CD79A), with AUC values (0.5970 for CD22, 0.5215 for CD79A) indicating limited diagnostic potential. Significant expression reductions were observed in blood samples associated with comorbidities (diabetes, hypertension, ischemic heart disease) and risk factors (smoking, alcohol), and different stages and genders (P < 0.05). A positive correlation between CD22 and CD79A expression was found (r = 0.3521, P = 0.0105). Although blood-based assessment of CD22 and CD79A showed no significant differences between patients and controls, significant expression alterations linked to metabolic comorbidities (e.g., diabetes) and environmental exposures (e.g., smoking) suggest their biological relevance in bladder cancer mechanisms. These findings highlight the compartment-specific expression of CD22 and CD79A and their possible relevance as candidate genes in blood in relation to comorbidities and risk factors.

title: Urinary Metabolic and Hemodynamic Protein Signatures in Canagliflozin Treated Patients With Diabetic Kidney Disease: Findings From CREDENCE.
abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) provide kidney protection in patients with diabetic kidney disease (DKD). There is limited knowledge about the mechanisms by which they protect the kidney. We investigated which urinary proteins and pathways are associated with progressive kidney disease and canagliflozin treatment. This case-control study included patients from the CREDENCE trial. Cases and controls were defined by annual eGFR decline of ≥ 5 or < 1 mL/min/1.73 m2 and propensity score-matched within treatment arms. High-throughput urinary proteomics (SomaLogic, n = 5284 aptamers) was performed at baseline and year 1. Differential abundance analysis assessed 1-year changes between cases and controls, and between canagliflozin and placebo-treated patients. Identified proteins were mapped to kidney biopsy single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from patients with type 2 diabetes, with or without SGLT2i treatment to identify cell type-specific expression. Of 392 included participants, 250 were randomized to canagliflozin and 142 to placebo. After 1 year, 124 proteins were changed by canagliflozin compared to placebo (92 increased and 32 decreased). Enolase 1, SLIT, NTRK Like Family Member 1, and leucine-rich repeat containing 15 increased more than 3-fold, while decreases were observed in alanyl aminopeptidase, discoidin domain receptor 1 and ameloblastin. Pathway analysis revealed enhanced activity of metabolic pathways. scRNA-seq data showed increased expression of metabolic genes after SGLT2i treatment in distal tubular cells. These findings suggest that SGLT2i administration induces a redistribution of tubular workload through compensatory sodium reabsorption in distal parts of the nephron, which may contribute to kidney-protective effects in DKD.

title: Comparative Evaluation of NaOCl/EDTA-Based Multi-Step Protocol Versus Triton-Based Single-Step Protocol on Reduction of Bacterial DNA and RNA Levels: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
abstract: Root canal irrigation plays a critical role in microbial reduction; however, culture-based methods may not fully detect residual microorganisms. This study compared the antibacterial efficacy of NaOCl/EDTA-based multi-step irrigation (MSIP) and Triton-based single-step irrigation (SSIP) protocols using molecular analysis. This double-blind study included 28 patients with maxillary central incisors diagnosed with pulp necrosis and asymptomatic apical periodontitis. Participants were randomized to group 1 (MSIP) and group 2 (SSIP) (n = 14 each). Bacterial samples were collected from the root canals before and after chemomechanical preparation (S1 and S2, respectively). All samples were placed in cryotubes containing RNAlater solution and transferred for molecular analysis. Data were analysed using Welch's t-test and two-way mixed-design repeated-measures ANOVA at p < 0.05. The reduction from S1 to S2 was significantly greater with SSIP than with MSIP for both log10-transformed DNA and RNA. The mean between-group difference in reduction (SSIP - MSIP) was 0.259 log10 units for DNA (95% CI, 0.120-0.398; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0009) and 0.508 log10 units for RNA (95% CI, 0.334-0.681; Holm-adjusted p < 0.0002). Complementary mixed-design repeated-measures ANOVA demonstrated significant time × group interactions for both DNA (p = 0.0006) and RNA (p < 0.0001). The Triton-based SSIP produced greater immediate reductions in bacterial DNA and RNA levels than the NaOCl/EDTA-based MSIP in maxillary central incisors with pulp necrosis and asymptomatic apical periodontitis. Triton-based SSIP may offer a simplified irrigation approach for root canal treatment, with potential antimicrobial benefits demonstrated under the clinical conditions evaluated in this study.

title: Iterative Geometric Structure Guided Nonnegative Matrix Factorization Scheme for Bulk Tissue RNA-seq Data Deconvolution.
abstract: Complete deconvolution is a class of unsupervised methods that aim to estimate both cell-type proportions and cell-type-specific gene expression profiles (GEPs) from bulk RNA-seq data, without requiring prior reference profiles. Hence, it enables broader applicability to tissues or species for which reference data are limited or unavailable. For many existing methods, nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) serves as the fundamental computational tool. However, NMF is mathematically ill-posed and a comprehensive understanding of how to overcome the inherent ill-posedness and improve solution accuracy remains lacking. In our previous work, we investigated the necessary requirements for a given bulk RNA-seq dataset to satisfy the solvability conditions in NMF theory. Based on its weak solvability conditions of NMF, a new pipeline of pseudo-bulk tissue data augmented, geometric structure guided NMF model (GSNMF+) has been developed. As a semi-supervised model, it utilizes available single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) data and has shown obvious improvements in scenarios where the target bulk data contain singular cellular compositions. Nevertheless, when the available scRNA-seq data are not fully consistent with the underlying cell-type-specific GEPs present in the bulk RNA-seq data, it remains a challenge that the deconvolution accuracy will significantly decrease. In this paper, we propose an iterative GSNMF algorithm to address this challenge. First, we propose a new computational algorithm for the GSNMF method (termed as the inner iteration) and provide a theoretical proof of its convergence. We then introduce an iterative process (termed as the outer iteration) to reduce potential discrepancies between available scRNA-seq and the latent cell type specific GEPs in the bulk-tissue data. The proposed methods are evaluated on both synthetic and realistic scRNA-seq data generated bulk-tissue datasets and have shown significant improvements in deconvolution accuracy, particularly in settings where the reference scRNA-seq data are inconsistent.

title: Identification of Proteomic Subtypes with Differential Responses to Immune Checkpoint Inhibition in Cutaneous Melanoma.
abstract: Predictive biomarkers for combined PD-1/CTLA-4 blockade in metastatic melanoma remain limited. We analyzed pretreatment proteogenomic data to define response and resistance biology. We profiled 208 pretreatment FFPE specimens from patients with metastatic cutaneous melanoma treated across 12 institutions, including 164 receiving dual PD-1+CTLA-4 blockade (Discovery, n=97; Validation 1, n=67) and 44 receiving PD-1 monotherapy. Tumors underwent TMT-based proteomics, RNA sequencing, and targeted/low-pass whole-genome sequencing. Pathway clustering, survival modeling, deconvolution, and machine-learning classification defined and validated subtype signatures. Proteomic pathway clustering identified three reproducible ICI subtypes: immune-enriched ICI-sensitive, ribosome-high, and EMT-like/stromal-enriched. Subtypes stratified progression-free survival after dual ICI in the Discovery (P=0.01) and Validation 1 cohorts (P=0.02). The ICI-sensitive subtype had the highest responder fraction (74% and 73%), compared with ribosome-high (67% and 60%) and EMT-like tumors (44% and 43%) in the Discovery and Validation 1 cohorts, respectively. Subtype-outcome associations were consistent with previous immunotherapy datasets, with pooled hazard ratios ≈0.5-0.8 for immune-enriched tumors. Subtypes plus clinical variables predicted 3-year progression/death better than clinical variables alone in Validation 1 (AUC 0.80 vs 0.64). A 127-protein classifier recapitulated subtype membership in Validation 1 (AUC 0.89-0.97) and predicted 3-year progression/death with AUC 0.79. Subtypes reflected distinct immune, translational, and stromal/ECM programs and nominated POLR3A-associated biology as a candidate resistance axis. Proteomic pathway states define reproducible, biologically interpretable melanoma subtypes associated with differential benefit from dual PD-1/CTLA-4 blockade. A clinically tractable 127-protein classifier provides a foundation for prospective biomarker-driven combination immunotherapy trials.

title: Deciphering the Mechanisms Underlying Therapeutic Resistance in Cancer through Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Technologies: Current Approaches and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics (ST) technologies are recent high-throughput sequencing advancements that enable transcriptome-wide profiling and characterization of cellular populations at single-cell resolution while preserving tissue spatial context. Their integration has been increasingly applied to cancer research, facilitating a deeper understanding of tumor biology and improving diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. Growing evidence suggests that combining single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with ST offers a robust approach for exploring mechanisms underlying therapeutic resistance. Together, these technologies support the prediction and monitoring of treatment responses and help identify novel therapeutic targets by revealing critical signaling pathways and immune cell populations associated with resistance. Artificial intelligence, including deep learning, computer vision, and generative models, further enhances the integration and analysis of data generated by scRNA-seq and ST, contributing to tumor resistance research. This review summarizes recent advances in the integrated application of scRNA-seq and ST to study tumor resistance and discusses the opportunities, challenges, and future directions of these technologies as a theoretical foundation for identifying therapeutic targets and developing treatment strategies.

title: Targeting Fibroblast Foxc2 Promotes Neurovascular Recovery by Suppressing Sdc4 After Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability, with current reperfusion therapies limited by narrow therapeutic windows and inability to promote sustained neurovascular repair. Here, we developed YZD-27, a rationally designed Tanshinone IIA (TSA) derivative with improved druggability, and show that it remains therapeutically effective when administered up to 24 h after ischemic injury in transient and permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO and dMCAO) mouse models. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and cell-cell communication analysis revealed broad cellular responses to YZD-27 and identified fibronectin-1 (Fn1)/syndecan-4 (Sdc4) as a predicted endothelia-fibroblast ligand-receptor interaction. Mechanistically, YZD-27 directly binds forkhead box protein C2 (Foxc2), enhances its protein stability by limiting proteasomal degradation, and increases its occupancy at the Sdc4 promoter, thereby repressing Sdc4 transcription in fibroblast. Fibroblast-conditioned medium experiments further supported a role for Foxc2/Sdc4 regulation in modulating endothelial barrier-related protein expression. These findings identify Foxc2/Sdc4 signaling as a regulatory mechanism associated with the therapeutic effects of YZD-27, and establish YZD-27 as a promising neurovascular therapeutic candidate for ischemic stroke.

title: PPARγ-Induced SUMOylation Drives Fbxo6-Mediated Cx43 Ubiquitination to Alleviate Osteoarthritis.
abstract: Previous studies from our group confirmed the chondroprotective effects of the PPARγ agonist pioglitazone. In the present study, we aimed to elucidate the mechanism by which PPARγ activation protects against osteoarthritis (OA), with a particular focus on the regulation of Connexin 43 (Cx43). OA models were established in mice and rats through exercise and intra-articular AGE-BSA injections. Cx43-knockout mice were used for genetic validation. Primary human and rat chondrocytes were treated with AGEs in vitro. Mechanistic investigations were performed using RNA-sequencing, co-immunoprecipitation, ubiquitination assays, cycloheximide chase assays, and functional tests. Cx43 expression was markedly upregulated in OA chondrocytes and inversely correlated with PPARγ levels. The PPARγ agonist pioglitazone alleviated OA and was accompanied by elevated PPARγ and reduced Cx43 protein levels without altering Cx43 mRNA levels. Genetic ablation of Cx43 attenuated OA severity, and under pioglitazone treatment, Cx43-KO mice did not exhibit additional protection compared with WT mice, whereas Cx43 overexpression reversed the drug's protection. Mechanistically, PPARγ activation promoted Cx43 degradation via a post-translational pathway. Integrated RNA-sequencing and IP-MS analyses identified SUMO2 and the E3 ligase adaptor Fbxo6 as key mediators of this process. Specifically, PPARγ upregulated SUMO2, which mediated Cx43 SUMOylation, facilitating its recognition by Fbxo6. This led to Cx43 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. Mutation of either Cx43 SUMOylation site (K109 or K133) or the disruption of the Fbxo6 SUMO-interacting motif (SIM) abolished this regulation. Functionally, activation of the SUMO2/Fbxo6 axis protected chondrocytes from AGEs-induced dysfunction. PPARγ activation triggers SUMO2-mediated Cx43 SUMOylation, thereby promoting Fbxo6-dependent ubiquitination and degradation of Cx43. This novel PPARγ-SUMO2-Fbxo6 axis is essential for chondroprotection, and provides new mechanistic insight and potential therapeutic targets for OA treatment. Clinical trial number: not applicable.

title: Oroxylin A attenuates pneumonia via HSP90α-dependent suppression of macrophage ferroptosis-mediated inflammation.
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the protective activity of Oroxylin A in pneumonia and to clarify the mechanisms involved, particularly those associated with macrophage-driven inflammation and ferroptosis. Pneumonia was induced in mice and treated with Oroxylin A, followed by evaluation of lung injury, inflammatory cytokine production, and ferroptosis-related markers. Pulmonary immune alterations were further characterized by single-cell RNA sequencing. Target-responsive accessibility profiling, molecular dynamics simulation, and cellular thermal shift assays were subsequently applied to explore potential molecular targets, followed by functional verification in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-challenged macrophages. Oroxylin A alleviated body weight loss, pathological lung injury, alveolar inflammation, and inflammatory cytokine production in mice with pneumonia. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis identified macrophages as a major responsive population and showed that Oroxylin A modulated inflammation- and ferroptosis-related transcriptional programs. In LPS-stimulated macrophages, Oroxylin A suppressed the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and increased GPX4 and SLC7A11 expression, whereas these effects were attenuated by erastin. Heat shock protein 90-alpha (HSP90α) was further identified as a potential binding target of Oroxylin A. In silico perturbation analyses suggested that HSP90α participates in ferroptosis-related biological processes. Functional experiments showed that HSP90α overexpression weakened the anti-inflammatory and anti-ferroptotic actions of Oroxylin A, whereas HSP90α knockdown suppressed inflammatory cytokine expression and increased GPX4 expression. Collectively, these findings suggest that Oroxylin A alleviates pneumonia-associated inflammation through an HSP90α-dependent mechanism involving the regulation of macrophage ferroptosis.

title: SH2B1 modulates hepatic lipid droplet homeostasis and is associated with HSC70/LAMP2A-related PLIN2 regulation in metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease.
abstract: SH2B adaptor protein 1 (SH2B1) participates in metabolic regulation, but its role in hepatic lipid-droplet homeostasis remains unclear. We investigated its role and underlying mechanisms in metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD). Human and mouse GEO transcriptomic datasets and liver single-cell RNA-sequencing data were analyzed to characterize SH2B1 expression and identify lipid-metabolism-related candidates. SH2B1 knockdown and overexpression were performed in palmitate/oleate (P/O)-treated AML12 hepatocytes, and lysosome-associated membrane protein 2 A (LAMP2A) knockdown was combined with SH2B1 overexpression to assess its functional contribution. Molecular docking explored potential interactions, while reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence assessed protein association and colocalization, respectively. In vivo, mice were fed a high-fat diet (HFD) and subsequently underwent AAV-mediated hepatic Sh2b1 knockdown. SH2B1 expression was reduced in human and murine fatty liver datasets and was predominantly detected in hepatocytes. Perilipin 2 (PLIN2) expression was inversely correlated with SH2B1 across GSE165855 samples. P/O exposure reduced SH2B1 expression and increased PLIN2 levels and lipid accumulation. SH2B1 knockdown increased PLIN2 abundance and lipid storage, whereas overexpression produced the opposite phenotype. Reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation supported an association between SH2B1 and heat shock cognate 70 (HSC70), and immunofluorescence demonstrated their colocalization. SH2B1 manipulation bidirectionally altered LAMP2A abundance. LAMP2A knockdown attenuated the reductions in PLIN2 abundance and lipid accumulation induced by SH2B1 overexpression. Hepatic Sh2b1 knockdown exacerbated HFD-induced hepatic lipid accumulation and liver injury, with lower LAMP2A and higher PLIN2 levels. SH2B1 regulates hepatic lipid-droplet homeostasis, with LAMP2A contributing to its effects on PLIN2 abundance and lipid accumulation.

title: Podocarpusflavone A sensitizes MASLD-related hepatocellular carcinoma to lenvatinib by targeting ABAT and ALDH2.
abstract: Despite the rising global incidence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease-related hepatocellular carcinoma (MASLD-HCC), immunotherapy offers limited survival benefits in this non-viral etiology, positioning lenvatinib as a critical treatment that necessitates novel strategies to enhance its efficacy. This study aimed to identify MASLD-HCC signature genes and to explore a novel agent to overcome lenvatinib resistance. Single-cell RNA sequencing identified signature genes, validated by immunohistochemistry, qPCR, Western blot, and spatial transcriptomics in human and murine specimens. Virtual screening identified a natural compound targeting hub genes. Direct binding was confirmed using molecular dynamics simulations, cellular thermal shift assays, and surface plasmon resonance. Therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms were comprehensively evaluated in vitro under lipotoxic stress conditions and in vivo using diet-induced orthotopic MASLD-HCC mouse models. A 170-gene signature was established, with ABAT and ALDH2 prioritized as hub genes. Podocarpusflavone A (PCFA) emerged as a dual-targeting agent that robustly reverses acquired lenvatinib resistance. Instead of increasing protein abundance, PCFA directly binds these targets, which is accompanied by markedly enhanced cellular ABAT and ALDH activities. This diminishes the protective GABA shield and disrupts the mitochondrial NAD⁺ balance, precipitating a lethal mitochondrial superoxide burst and inhibiting key oncogenic pathways. In vivo, the PCFA and lenvatinib combination profoundly suppressed orthotopic tumor progression and was associated with short-term improvements in hepatic steatosis and fibrosis-related histological findings, with no evident toxicity under the conditions tested. PCFA combined with lenvatinib represents a promising strategy for MASLD-HCC and provides mechanistic insights into its antitumor activity.

title: Cross-cohort analyses of OLFML2B cellular distribution and stromal associations in gastric adenocarcinoma.
abstract: OLFML2B has been associated with gastric cancer, but the cellular basis and clinical transportability of its tissue-level signal remain uncertain. Following a five-cohort screen and literature-informed prioritisation, we evaluated bulk, single-cell, spatial and proteomic datasets and an anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1)-treated cohort using question-specific preprocessing and an explicit evidence hierarchy. The Cancer Genome Atlas stomach adenocarcinoma cohort showed higher tumour expression, including 33 paired comparisons (median log2-scale difference 2.28; P = 1.951 × 10⁻⁵). Random-effects meta-analyses of Spearman rank correlations across five follow-up cohorts linked OLFML2B with fibroblast, extracellular-matrix and transforming-growth-factor-beta programmes (summary correlations 0.73, 0.69 and 0.56). Heterogeneity was substantial and all prediction intervals included zero. Among 413,873 reprocessed single cells, patient-level estimates were higher for fibroblast than epithelial detection in two primary comparisons, but did not establish higher fibroblast than myeloid detection; one epithelial contrast was sensitive to detection thresholds and ambient-RNA correction. Spatial associations in nine patients provided stromal context. Only one cohort supported the common-adjustment recurrence model. Secondary overall-survival meta-analysis of three commonly adjusted cohorts yielded a hazard ratio of 1.27 (95% confidence interval 1.01-1.59), with wider intervals after cohort omission. In 30 qualified proteomic pairs, the Wilcoxon analysis supported a positive location shift (Hodges-Lehmann estimate 0.380, 95% confidence interval 0.024-0.654; P = 0.0397), with plex sensitivity. Response associations in 45 anti-PD-1-treated patients remained imprecise. These findings support a stromal-associated expression context while leaving cellular function, residual confounding and clinical transportability unresolved. Cohort disagreement does not establish absence of biological or clinical effects.

title: The role of m6A reader YTHDF2 in lymphangiogenesis via RNF43/WNT5B in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Lymphangiogenesis significantly contributes to poor prognosis and reduced survival in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) patients due to lymphatic metastasis. Despite the critical role of N6-methyladenosine (m6A)-the most abundant eukaryotic mRNA modification-its influence on OSCC lymphangiogenesis and metastasis remains poorly understood. This study identifies YTHDF2, a key m6A reader protein, as markedly upregulated in OSCC and strongly correlated with advanced nodal staging (N-staging). In vitro experiments revealed that YTHDF2 enhances OSCC cell migration and invasion while promoting tube formation and migration in human lymphatic endothelial cells (HLECs). In vivo experiments showed that silencing YTHDF2 reduced lymphatic vessel density in orthotopic tumors and suppressed cervical lymph node metastasis. Mechanistically, integrated RNA-seq and m6A-seq data linked YTHDF2-regulated genes to the WNT pathway. YTHDF2 directly binds m6A-modified RNF43 mRNA, accelerating its decay and upregulating WNT5B expression. Our findings indicate that WNT5B serves as an important contributor to lymphangiogenesis and lymphatic metastasis in OSCC. These findings elucidate the role of YTHDF2 in OSCC metastasis via m6A dependent regulation of the RNF43-WNT5B axis. In addition, WNT5B appears to contribute to lymphangiogenesis signaling, and these findings point toward the YTHDF2-RNF43-WNT5B pathway as a subject of interest for future therapeutic exploration in OSCC.

title: A Th17-centered immune network for tertiary lymphoid structure formation in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma after neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy.
abstract: Neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (NICT) benefits esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), yet underlying antitumor immunity remains elusive. This study aimed to dissect the cellular and molecular determinants and identify predictive biomarkers of NICT response in ESCC. Longitudinal single-cell RNA and T/B cell receptor sequencing was performed on paired pre- and post-NICT ESCC samples from 20 patients. Spatial analyses and functional assays were employed to investigate the compartmentalized distribution and functional adaptation of cells within ESCC tumor microenvironment in response to NICT. Through single-cell multi-omics profiling of ESCC tumors, we identified Th17 accumulation accompanied by IL-22 and IL-17A upregulation in responders after NICT. IL-22 promoted differentiation of IL22RA1+ cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) into CCL19+ CAFs and tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) formation. Th17-derived IL-17A primed B cells differentiation toward the TNFSF9+ B trajectory with increased antibody production. Pretreatment quantification of IL22RA1⁺ fibroblasts predicted NICT response in ESCC. In mice, hydroxycholesterols or IL-17A and IL-22 supplementation induced TLS formation and improved immunochemotherapy efficacy. Our work delineates a Th17-CAF-B cell axis critical for TLS neogenesis and NICT response in ESCC, providing mechanism-based biomarkers for patient stratification and strategies to overcome treatment resistance.

title: Integrative Multi-Omics and Structure-based Analysis of DHODH Reveals its Therapeutic Potential in Colorectal Cancer.
abstract: Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH) is a mitochondrial enzyme involved in de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis and has emerged as a potential target in cancer metabolism and therapy. This study integrated transcriptomic analysis with structure-based drug discovery to investigate the biological significance and therapeutic potential of DHODH in colorectal cancer (COAD and READ). TCGA-COAD and TCGA-READ RNA-seq data were analyzed for differential expression, clinical association, survival, pathway enrichment, immune infiltration, and therapeutic relevance, with GSE44076 used for external validation. DHODH was significantly elevated in colorectal cancer, while its expression showed limited association with overall survival. Enrichment and immune analyses suggested that DHODH may be associated with immune-related processes and the tumor immune microenvironment. CCLE/DepMap analysis further indicated DHODH dependency in a subset of colorectal cancer cell lines. Structure-based virtual screening identified several promising compounds, including (+)-Luguine, Benzyl 2-[(2-cinnamylidene-3-oxo-1-benzofuran-6-yl)oxy]acetate, 2,3,5-trimethyl-6-(3-(4-methylpiperazin-1-yl)-3-oxopropyl)-7H-furo[3,2-g]chromen-7-one, and N-[2-(4-methylphenyl)ethyl]-2-(2-oxo-1,2-dihydroquinolin-3-yl)acetamide. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations supported stable ligand-DHODH interactions. MM/PBSA analysis showed favorable binding free energies ranging from -4.98 to -7.69 kcal/mol, with the DHODH-(+)-Luguine complex exhibiting the most favorable predicted binding energy. ADMET analysis further indicated generally acceptable drug-like and pharmacokinetic properties, although compound-specific toxicity concerns were identified. Overall, DHODH may represent a promising therapeutic target in colorectal cancer, while the identified compounds provide potential candidates for further experimental validation as DHODH inhibitors.

title: An APOA5-Derived Signature Bridges Cholesterol Homeostasis to T-Cell Exhaustion and Directs Lung Adenocarcinoma Immunotherapy Response.
abstract: Immune heterogeneity and metabolic remodeling frequently limit the efficacy of immunotherapy in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). To address this challenge, we integrated single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing analyses, pairing machine learning with preclinical models to develop the APOA5-correlated T-cell Signature (ACTsig), which effectively stratifies LUAD patients and predicts immunotherapeutic response. Moreover, We identified apolipoprotein A-V (APOA5) as a previously unrecognized tumor suppressor linking cholesterol homeostasis to the tumor immune ecosystem. Mechanistically, APOA5 deficiency induced intracellular cholesterol accumulation and MIF production. Cholesterol depletion and replenishment established a causal role for cholesterol accumulation in regulating MIF production, while MIF knockdown reversed APOA5-loss-induced T-cell exhaustion and recombinant MIF restored the phenotype. Meanwhile, CXCR4 blockade rescued APOA5-loss-induced T-cell exhaustion, supporting the functional involvement of the MIF receptor CXCR4 in this immunosuppressive phenotype. Finally, in silico drug screening identified fenofibrate, which, in combination with anti-PD-1 therapy, significantly suppressed tumor growth in APOA5-deficient models. Together, these findings establish ACTsig as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy response and reveal an APOA5-cholesterol-MIF-CXCR4 axis underlying T-cell exhaustion.

title: Unraveling the role of MCM7 in cancer: a comprehensive analysis and functional validation from pan-cancer to lung adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Minichromosome maintenance protein 7 (MCM7), an integral component of the DNA replication licensing complex, has been implicated in diverse human malignancies. However, a holistic, multi-omics evaluation of its oncogenic repertoire across a broad spectrum of cancers remains conspicuously absent. We comprehensively characterized the expression landscape, prognostic significance, genetic aberrations, and immunomodulatory correlations of MCM7 across 33 cancer types, and further experimentally corroborated its functional and mechanistic roles in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). We leveraged multi-omics datasets from TCGA, GTEx, CPTAC, and HPA to assess MCM7 expression, survival outcomes, and genomic alterations. Correlative analyses were performed with tumor mutational burden, microsatellite instability, cancer-associated fibroblast infiltration, immune checkpoints, and RNA modification regulators. Functionally, MCM7 was silenced via siRNA in LUAD cell lines, followed by comprehensive assessments of proliferation, cell cycle, migration, invasion, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Mechanistic exploration was conducted via RNA-sequencing and western blotting. MCM7 is markedly upregulated in most malignant tumors, and its elevated expression is closely associated with poor survival prognosis. Copy number amplification was identified as the predominant genetic alteration, while the R72C/H mutation was specifically linked to dismal outcomes in glioblastoma. Notably, MCM7 expression displayed robust positive correlations with TMB, MSI, the immune checkpoint HMGB1, and the m5C reader ALYREF in most cancer types. Functional enrichment reaffirmed its canonical involvement in cell cycle and DNA replication. In vitro, MCM7 knockdown drastically abrogated LUAD cell viability, colony formation, and metastatic capacity, while inducing G0/G1 phase arrest and reversing EMT phenotypes. Mechanistically, transcriptomic and experimental validations convergently revealed that MCM7 silencing exerts its anti-tumor effects via suppression of the JAK-STAT3 signaling cascade. Our findings establish MCM7 as a bona fide pan cancer oncogenic determinant and a promising diagnostic/prognostic biomarker. Furthermore, we unveil a novel mechanistic axis linking MCM7 to JAK STAT3 driven inflammatory signaling in LUAD, offering a pre-clinical hypothesis for targeting MCM7 in combination with immunotherapeutic or JAK/STAT inhibitory regimens, although in-vivo validation and toxicity assessment remain essential.

title: Identification of IFI44L as a potential immune-associated molecule and theoretical CAR-T target for systemic lupus erythematosus: a cross-platform bioinformatic analysis.
abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a highly heterogeneous autoimmune disorder characterized by disrupted immune homeostasis, persistent chronic inflammation, and progressive multi-organ injury, accompanied by frequent disease flares and marked interindividual clinical heterogeneity. At present, specific molecular biomarkers for precise evaluation of immune dysregulation and guidance for individualized targeted therapy for SLE remain scarce. This study aimed to screen core genes associated with SLE, explore the correlation between IFI44L and SLE-associated immune disturbance, and validate its diagnostic performance, so as to provide bioinformatic evidence for precise immune diagnosis and targeted intervention of SLE. The GSE72326 microarray dataset was used as the training cohort to screen differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between SLE patients and healthy controls. Gene Ontology (GO), Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analyses were performed to identify core hub genes. The CIBERSORTx algorithm was adopted to quantify peripheral blood immune cell infiltration. Spearman correlation analysis was conducted to assess the association between hub gene expression and immune cell infiltration, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were plotted to evaluate gene diagnostic efficacy. An independent RNA-seq cohort GSE211700 was used for cross-platform external validation of IFI44L expression patterns and diagnostic efficacy. A total of 104 SLE-related DEGs, including 93 upregulated and 11 downregulated genes, were identified with distinct expression patterns capable of distinguishing SLE patients from healthy controls. Functional enrichment results revealed that DEGs were predominantly enriched in type I interferon response, innate immune activation and inflammatory signaling cascades, consistent with the well-recognized pathological features of SLE. As a key interferon-stimulated gene, IFI44L was selected as the primary target based on integrated transcriptomic profiles and previous mechanistic evidence, despite several other hub genes exhibiting larger expression fold changes. Correlation analysis demonstrated that elevated IFI44L expression was significantly positively correlated with the proportions of M1 macrophages and activated NK cells, and negatively correlated with naive B cells and neutrophils (all P < 0.001). Dual-cohort ROC analysis confirmed the diagnostic potential of IFI44L, with AUCs of 0.9032 in the training cohort and 0.9550 in the independent validation cohort. Consistent with transcriptomic enrichment results, IFI44L may correlate with type I interferon pathway disturbance and abnormal peripheral immune cell infiltration linked to inflammatory manifestations in SLE. Validated across two independent cross-platform cohorts, IFI44L may serve as a non-invasive diagnostic biomarker for SLE. Its potential as a CAR-T target is merely a theoretical conjecture derived from bioinformatic analysis, which provides preliminary clues for subsequent research on individualized treatment of refractory SLE. Key Points • Cross-platform validation using microarray and RNA-seq datasets verified consistent upregulation of peripheral blood IFI44L in SLE patients. • Elevated IFI44L expression correlates with peripheral blood immune cell infiltration disorders and bioinformatically inferred enrichment of type I interferon associated transcriptional signatures in SLE cohorts. • IFI44L exhibits acceptable diagnostic performance for SLE and may serve as a non-invasive blood-based biomarker for SLE. Its potential as a CAR-T target remains only a bioinformatics-derived hypothesis.

title: Multidimensional Deciphering Underlying Effects of PFOA Exposure in Ulcerative Colitis: From Epidemiological Insights to Toxicological Mechanisms.
abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), a representative persistent organic pollutant (POP), has been linked to numerous adverse health effects. Ulcerative colitis (UC), characterized by recurrent colon inflammation, is known to have environmental exposure as a primary etiological factor; however, the toxicological mechanisms underlying PFOA-induced UC remain unclear. This study therefore aims to comprehensively investigate the association between PFOA exposure and UC. A meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate the association between PFOA exposure and UC onset, and network toxicology, cross-species transcriptomics, protein-protein interaction networks, and weighted gene coexpression network analysis were employed to identify potential targets and mechanisms. Single-cell RNA sequencing, molecular docking, and Mendelian randomization were used to pinpoint and validate hub genes, while in vivo DSS-induced colitis and in vitro inflammation models were applied to assess the functional impact of PFOA. The meta-analysis of four studies confirmed a significant positive association between PFOA exposure and UC risk (Fisher z = 0.20, 95% CI: 0.13-0.27). We identified 170 overlapping targets linking PFOA to UC, predominantly enriched in immune-inflammatory activation and metabolic disruption. Seven hub genes (IRF1, CXCL1, CXCL9, CXCL10, CXCL11, CASP1, and IL1B) constituted a UC-associated coexpression module, with monocytes/macrophages as primary sources by single-cell profiling. Molecular docking confirmed PFOA binding to these proteins, and Mendelian randomization established IRF1 as a causal risk factor. In vivo, PFOA exacerbated DSS-induced colitis, impairing barrier function, promoting apoptosis and mitochondrial dysfunction. In conclusion, PFOA exposure is associated with increased UC risk and may promote colonic inflammation by affecting the chemokine-inflammasome network and epithelial function.
