IRF1 may be a key hub in this process, but its upstream role needs validation. These findings highlight the potential importance of reducing environmental pollutant exposure in UC prevention.

title: Plasma proteins and antibody immune responses in non-small cell lung cancer: Evidence from Mendelian randomization, mediation analysis, and single-cell transcriptomics.
abstract: ObjectiveTo investigate the potential causal relationships between circulating plasma proteins and non-small cell lung cancer and to assess whether antibody immune response traits mediate these associations.MethodsWe conducted an integrative genetic epidemiology study combining two-sample Mendelian randomization, mediation analysis, single-cell transcriptomics, and tissue-based experimental validation. Plasma protein data for 4907 proteins and genome-wide association study summary statistics for 46 antibody immune response traits were analyzed alongside non-small cell lung cancer genome-wide association study data from 218,792 individuals of European ancestry (1627 cases and 217,165 controls). Five complementary Mendelian randomization methods were applied; sensitivity analyses assessed heterogeneity, horizontal pleiotropy, and robustness, and reverse Mendelian randomization assessed potential reverse causation. Mediation analysis evaluated antibody immune response traits as candidate intermediate phenotypes. Prioritized proteins were further characterized using single-cell RNA sequencing data and paired tumor and adjacent normal tissues from patients with histopathologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer.ResultsWe identified 1188 plasma proteins with potential causal associations with non-small cell lung cancer risk. CLEC10A and TGM3 were prioritized through sequential plasma protein-non-small cell lung cancer, plasma protein-antibody immune response, and mediation analyses. Higher genetically predicted CLEC10A levels were associated with increased non-small cell lung cancer risk, whereas higher genetically predicted TGM3 levels were associated with lower non-small cell lung cancer risk. Five antibody immune response traits were initially associated with non-small cell lung cancer, of which four were retained after robustness assessment. Mediation analysis identified three candidate plasma protein-antibody immune response-non-small cell lung cancer pathways involving GCST90006921 and GCST90006923. Single-cell analysis localized CLEC10A and TGM3 predominantly to macrophages, while paired tissue analyses showed higher CLEC10A and lower TGM3 expression in tumors.ConclusionsCLEC10A and TGM3 may contribute to non-small cell lung cancer susceptibility, with specific antibody immune response traits representing candidate intermediate immune pathways. These findings provide genetic and complementary biological support for further independent replication and mechanistic investigation.

title: ACSL5 suppresses pancreatic cancer progression and gemcitabine resistance by regulating n-6 docosapentaenoic acid metabolism.
abstract: Gemcitabine (GEM) resistance remains a major challenge in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) treatment. Metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of tumors, and imbalance in lipid metabolism promotes tumor progression and drug resistance. This study aims to elucidate the mechanism of Acyl-CoA Synthetase Long Chain Family Member 5 (ACSL5) in PDAC, its impact on fatty acid metabolism, and its clinical relevance. Through RNA sequencing, targeted metabolomics, proteomics, retrospective cohort studies, and a series of in vitro and in vivo experiments, the significance of ACSL5 was systematically investigated. Our results showed that ACSL5 was downregulated in GEM-resistant cells, and its high expression predicted better survival in PDAC patients. ACSL5 overexpression suppressed proliferation, migration, invasion, and GEM resistance in PDAC cells, while its knockdown promoted these phenotypes. ACSL5 may exert its effects through the PPARδ/CPT1A signaling pathway, thereby influencing fatty acid β-oxidation. Notably, ACSL5 selectively modulated n-6 docosapentaenoic acid (DPA-n6) levels, while prospective cohort studies have shown that high plasma DPA-n6 is an independent risk factor for poor prognosis. Junction Plakoglobin (JUP) was identified as an ACSL5-binding protein and was associated with ACSL5 ubiquitination and protein stability. In summary, ACSL5 acts as a tumor suppressor in PDAC by modulating fatty acid metabolism. DPA-n6 may serve as a novel prognostic biomarker, highlighting the clinical relevance of ACSL5-associated lipid metabolism in PDAC.

title: A prognostic model based on platelet-related genes accurately predicts survival in patients with gastric cancer.
abstract: Platelets contribute to gastric cancer (GC) progression and metastasis. In this study, we aimed to construct a prognostic model based on platelet-related genes (PRGs) to predict outcomes in GC. RNA sequencing data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes, from which PRGs were selected as candidates. A prognostic model was built using machine learning. Immune infiltration was evaluated with CIBERSORT, and Spearman correlation was used to assess the relationships between prognostic PRGs and immune cells. Single-cell transcriptomics was used to explore cellular expression patterns, and molecular regulatory networks were constructed. The expression of candidate genes was validated in cell lines by reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). A total of 8,387 differentially expressed genes, including 123 PRGs, were identified. An eight-gene prognostic model (THPO, MMRN1, EGF, SPARC, GNAI1, CD36, SERPINE1, and ADAMTS18) was established. Distinct immune infiltration patterns were observed between risk groups, with differences in M2 macrophages, monocytes, neutrophils, activated memory CD4+ T cells, regulatory T cells, and follicular helper T cells. MMRN1 expression correlated positively with monocytes (r = 0.37), whereas GNAI1 expression was negatively associated with activated memory CD4+ T cells (r = - 0.30). Single-cell analysis showed that prognostic genes were mainly expressed in epithelial cells and fibroblasts. Two regulatory axes, SPARC-hsa-miR-494-3p-NEAT1 and GNAI1-hsa-miR-4262-NEAT1, were implicated in GC progression. RT-qPCR confirmed downregulation of CD36 and upregulation of SERPINE1 in GC tissues. This platelet-related gene model predicts survival and immune infiltration in GC and may support the development of personalized therapies.

title: RAB13 promotes diffuse large B-cell lymphoma progression and reduces lenalidomide sensitivity via PIK3CA-associated PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling.
abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is a biologically heterogeneous malignancy with variable clinical outcomes and treatment responses. Although the small GTPase RAB13 has been implicated in several cancers, its clinical significance, biological function, and relationship to lenalidomide (LEN) sensitivity in DLBCL remain unclear. Exploratory drug-sensitivity prediction was performed using the TCGA-DLBC cohort, and RAB13 expression and clinical associations were evaluated in tissue samples from 80 patients with non-GCB DLBCL. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments were conducted in two ABC-DLBCL cell lines, followed by RNA sequencing, protein-association analyses, genetic and pharmacological inhibition of PIK3CA/PI3K signaling, and xenograft studies. High RAB13 expression was associated with high-risk clinicopathological features and poorer survival in the non-GCB DLBCL cohort and was more frequent in patients with refractory or relapsed disease in the LEN-treated subgroup. In ABC-DLBCL cell models, RAB13 overexpression increased proliferation, Transwell migration and invasion, and reduced apoptosis, whereas RAB13 knockdown showed reciprocal effects. RAB13 overexpression also reduced LEN sensitivity, whereas RAB13 knockdown increased it. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses implicated PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling. RAB13 and PIK3CA were detected in the same protein complex, and PIK3CA knockdown or pharmacological PI3K inhibition attenuated RAB13-associated AKT-mTOR activation and pro-survival phenotypes. Alpelisib enhanced LEN-induced apoptosis in RAB13-overexpressing cells. In vivo, RAB13 overexpression accelerated xenograft growth, whereas RAB13 knockdown suppressed it. LEN combined with LY294002 reduced the growth of RAB13-overexpressing xenografts. RAB13 is associated with aggressive clinical features and poorer survival in non-GCB DLBCL and experimentally reduces LEN sensitivity in ABC-DLBCL models. These effects involve PIK3CA and PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling, supporting further evaluation of RAB13 as a candidate prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target.

title: NOTCH3/JAG1 signaling is associated with immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment features in ovarian cancer: links to nutritional risk, CD163+ macrophages, and CD8+ T cell exclusion.
abstract: NOTCH3 signaling is frequently dysregulated in ovarian cancer and has been linked to tumor progression and treatment resistance. We investigated the prognostic significance of NOTCH3 expression and its associations with immune-cell infiltration, nutritional risk, tumor-associated biomarkers, and transcriptional programs in public single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets. We retrospectively analyzed 186 patients with epithelial ovarian cancer stratified by immunohistochemistry-assessed NOTCH3 expression (n = 93 per group). Clinicopathological variables, nutritional measures (BMI, serum albumin, and NRS-2002), tumor-associated biomarkers (CA-125 and HE4), immune markers (CD8+, CD4+, CD163+, FOXP3+, and PD-L1), treatment response, and survival were evaluated. Public scRNA-seq datasets were used for complementary exploratory analysis of NOTCH3-associated transcriptional patterns. NOTCH3-high expression was associated with shorter overall survival, lower CD8+ TIL density, higher CD163+ tumor-associated macrophage density, lower chemotherapy response, and higher platinum resistance. High nutritional risk and hypoalbuminaemia were also associated with an immune-excluded phenotype after adjustment for clinicopathological covariates. The combined NOTCH3-high/NRS-2002 ≥ 3 subgroup had the poorest observed clinical outcomes. In the scRNA-seq analysis, epithelial cells showed the highest NOTCH3-related signature scores, and JAG1 showed the strongest co-expression with NOTCH3 among the evaluated ligands. These findings are associative and do not establish functional ligand-receptor signaling or a causal nutrition-mediated mechanism. High NOTCH3 expression is associated with an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, adverse treatment response, and poorer survival in ovarian cancer. Nutritional risk identifies an additional clinically relevant correlate of immune and survival outcomes. The observational clinical design and exploratory public scRNA-seq analysis do not establish causality; functional validation and prospective studies are required before specific nutritional or NOTCH3-targeted interventions can be recommended.

title: Single-cell analysis reveals transcriptomic patterns in active macrophage activation syndrome and therapeutic potential of albumin-fused interleukin-10 in a mouse model.
abstract: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) and macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) are life-threatening hyperinflammatory conditions. We aimed to characterize immune cell transcriptomic patterns in human MAS and investigate the therapeutic potential of albumin-fused IL-10 protein (SA-IL-10) in a MAS mouse model. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on bone marrow and peripheral blood samples from patients with newly developed MAS caused by diverse etiologies. We generated paired Seq-Well single-cell transcriptomes from bone marrow and blood of patients with active HLH/MAS. In the absence of a contemporaneous control cohort, technology-matched public Seq-Well marrow and same-laboratory control blood were projected onto the frozen patient atlases as lineage context, not as a case-control comparison. We also evaluated the effect of SA-IL-10 in a CpG-DNA-induced mouse model of MAS. Human scRNA-seq identified diverse immune cell populations, including dendritic cells, macrophages, and monocyte subsets. Canonical lineages in the public data were transferred to the expected patient states. Monocyte 1 and macrophage populations expressed transcripts encoding IL-10 receptor subunits and associated signaling molecules, although these findings reflect RNA abundance and do not establish functional responsiveness. Donor-level phagocytosis and interferon-γ programs showed no significant differences after multiple-testing correction. In the mouse model, SA-IL-10 treatment significantly improved anemia, leukocytopenia, splenomegaly, and liver dysfunction and was associated with reduced circulating interferon-γ levels and bone marrow macrophage abundance. Human scRNA-seq provides transcriptomic patterns in active HLH/MAS. The therapeutic effects observed in the mouse model support further investigation of SA-IL-10 as a potential treatment for MAS.

title: Rationale and design of the Cardiac MRI and Biological Samples in the Acute Phase of ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction study (the CARAMBOLE study).
abstract: ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) can lead to complications such as no-reflow/microvascular obstruction (MVO) and left ventricular remodeling (LVR), both with major prognostic impact. Inflammation is central to these mechanisms, and gut dysbiosis may amplify it through elevated trimethylamine N-oxide and lipopolysaccharides. A multiparametric strategy integrating cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), microbiome profiling and immuno-inflammatory biomarkers may improve the understanding and prediction of these complications. CARAMBOLE is a prospective, single-centre translational cohort study. From March 2024 to July 2025, 150 consecutive STEMI patients at Poitiers University Hospital were included. Eligible patients (≥18 years, confirmed STEMI, informed consent, no CMR contraindication) underwent serial blood sampling and biobanking (plasma, serum, PBMCs, DNA, RNA) at admission, 24 h and 48 h. Faecal and urinary sampling for gut and genitourinary microbiome characterisation, standardised questionnaires (lifestyle, quality of life, cognitive assessment), echocardiography, and CMR were performed during the acute phase and repeated at 1-year follow-up. The primary objective is to identify clinical, biological and imaging biomarkers associated with 1-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: cardiovascular death, recurrent myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, heart-failure hospitalisation), adjudicated by an independent blinded committee. Multi-omic analyses (shotgun metagenomics, targeted metabolomics, high-plex inflammatory proteomics) are pre-specified as exploratory and several are contingent on additional funding. This multiparametric, translational cohort will provide new mechanistic and epidemiological insights into the relationships among dysbiosis, inflammation, and CMR markers (no-reflow/MVO, infarct size, LVR), with the goal of generating prognostic biomarker hypotheses to be validated in larger, multicentre cohorts.

title: Super-enhancer-dependent transcriptional and m⁶A-mediated post-transcriptional regulation cooperatively drive lncRNA H19 to promote ESCC progression.
abstract: Epigenetic dysregulation mediated by long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), super-enhancers (SEs), and m⁶A modification remains incompletely characterized in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). ChIP-qPCR, dual-luciferase reporter assays and CRISPRi were performed to investigate the transcriptional regulation mechanism of H19 by super-enhancer. The functions and downstream signal transduction mechanisms of the H19 in ESCC were explored by a series of in vitro and in vivo assays, including RNA stability, RIP-qPCR, and MeRIP-qPCR. Furthermore, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and pseudotime trajectory analysis were used to analyze its correlation with ESCC patient survival. We identified H19, a super-enhancer-driven lncRNA, as a critical oncogenic factor in ESCC, with its overexpression significantly correlating with poor patient prognosis. Mechanistically, the master transcription factor KLF5 binds the super-enhancer region of H19 locus to drive its transcriptional activation. Post-transcriptionally, H19 interacts with the m⁶A methylation reader protein IGF2BP2, which stabilizes H19 in an m⁶A-dependent manner mediated by METTL3. The resulting H19/IGF2BP2 complex upregulates the oncogenic Tweety family member 3 (TTYH3) by enhancing mRNA stability. Functional assays revealed that the H19/IGF2BP2-TTYH3 axis facilitates ESCC malignant progression, while the IGF2BP2 inhibitor CWI1-2 suppresses tumorigenesis. ScRNA-seq combined with pseudotime trajectory analysis further established a significant positive correlation between METTL3/IGF2BP2/TTYH3 expression and malignant phenotypes in ESCC. The H19/IGF2BP2-TTYH3 axis drives ESCC progression, providing valuable prognostic biomarkers and promising therapeutic targets for ESCC treatment.

title: A ten-gene tyrosine-metabolism signature defines prognosis and reveals metabo-immune suppression in low-grade astrocytoma.
abstract: Emerging evidence implicates dysregulated tyrosine metabolism in glioma malignancy; however, its cell-type specificity and clinical relevance in low-grade astrocytoma (LGA) remain undefined. We integrated single-cell transcriptomes from two independent LGA cohorts (GSE182109 and GSE222850) and mapped tyrosine-metabolic activity across the tumor microenvironment using GSVA. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) of bulk RNA-seq data was performed to identify a tyrosine metabolism-associated gene module, from which hub genes were extracted. A total of 101 machine learning algorithm combinations were systematically evaluated to construct a prognostic signature, which was subsequently validated in the REMBRANDT and CGGA LGA cohorts. Multidimensional functional analyses, immune deconvolution, CellChat-based intercellular communication analysis, and in vitro functional assays were employed to characterize the underlying biological programs and therapeutic implications. At single-cell resolution, tyrosine metabolism activity was preferentially enriched in astrocytes and exhibited dynamic variation along pseudotime trajectories. WGCNA identified a turquoise module (r = 0.61, p = 4 × 10-16), from which 12 hub genes were identified by univariate Cox regression. A Lasso + CoxBoost-based 10-gene tyrosine metabolism risk model was constructed through systematic evaluation of 101 algorithm combinations. High risk scores independently predicted unfavorable 5-year overall survival (AUC = 0.80 in REMBRANDT; AUC = 0.73 in CGGA). High-risk tumors exhibited activation of interferon-γ response, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), E2F targets, and G2M checkpoint pathways. Immune profiling revealed significantly elevated infiltration of M2 macrophages and activated mast cells in the high-risk group. CellChat analysis demonstrated that high-risk astrocytes engage in intercellular communication via MIF, PTN, and SPP1 signaling pathways. Functional validation in MOG-G-UVW cells confirmed that RAB3C knockdown significantly promoted migration, invasion, and proliferation (p < 0.0001). We present a single-cell-resolved, clinically validated tyrosine metabolism-based prognostic signature for LGA. This risk model enables quantitative patient stratification, reveals a metabolically reprogrammed and immune-suppressive tumor microenvironment, and identifies RAB3C as a tumor-suppressive modulator, thereby offering new avenues for the precision management of low-grade astrocytoma.
